    Software Testing & QA Automation
    Department Handbook

    From zero to professional: onboarding, training, client QA delivery, automation, performance, costing, metrics and release sign-off

    Issued by VEL Software Solutions

    velsoftwaresolutions.in@gmail.com

    Document VEL-QA-001 · Version 1.0 (draft for management approval) · Issued 4 November 2026
    Tool versions, licences, limits and prices change. Always verify against official documentation and vendor pricing before training, building or quoting. Confidential · internal use.

    How to Use This Handbook

    This document is the single operating manual for the Software Testing & QA Automation Department. It does two jobs: (1) it trains a beginner from zero to a professional who can join supervised client projects, and (2) it defines the mandatory 16-stage QA lifecycle every client project follows, with procedures, templates, evidence requirements and approval gates.

    Golden rules
    1. Do not skip stages. Do not start a stage until the previous stage's approval gate is signed.
    2. Evidence or it did not happen. Every pass, fail, blocked or skipped result needs reproducible evidence (screenshot, log, HAR file, report or recording) stored in the project repository.
    3. Test only systems you are authorised in writing to test. Never test production or third-party systems without the client's written approval.
    4. Security testing is limited to authorised assessment activity and is coordinated with qualified security personnel. Testers report suspected vulnerabilities; they do not exploit them.
    5. Never commit passwords, API keys, tokens, customer personal data or production database extracts.
    6. Never manipulate, round up, or selectively report metrics to make a project look successful. Report unresolved risk honestly.
    7. Never claim software is “bug-free”, “secure” or “guaranteed”. Testing reduces risk; it cannot prove the absence of defects.
    8. Every release recommendation needs a second reviewer (QA Lead) before it reaches the client.

    Reading path for a beginner

    Part A: Learn (Levels 1–6)→Part B: Tools→Part C: Client lifecycle (16 stages)→Part D: Repository, documents, metrics→Part E: Costing & roles→Part F: Projects, plan, assessment

    The teaching method used for every topic

    Each learning topic is delivered in the same ten parts so that nothing is left to chance. Trainers must not mark a topic complete until all ten parts are done.

    #PartWhat the trainee must receive or produce
    1DefinitionA one- or two-sentence plain-language definition, plus the formal term (ISTQB glossary where one exists).
    2PurposeWhy the topic matters to a client and what risk it reduces.
    3SetupTools, accounts, test data and environment needed before starting.
    4ProcedureNumbered steps the trainee follows exactly.
    5Expected outputWhat the finished work must look like (file, report, screenshot, command output).
    6VerificationHow the trainee proves the work is correct (self-check list or peer check).
    7ErrorsThe most common mistakes and how to recognise and fix them.
    8ReportingHow and where the result is recorded (template, repo path, defect tracker).
    9AssignmentA practical task, time-boxed, with deliverables.
    10AssessmentPass criteria: a quiz, a demonstration, or a reviewed deliverable.

    1. Company Service Portfolio

    Seventeen commercially deliverable services. Each can be sold alone or combined into a project, a fixed-scope package, a time-based engagement or a monthly retainer (see Costing and Pricing).

    ServiceWhat we deliverTypical client triggerPrimary roles
    Manual software testingRisk-based test design, scripted and exploratory execution, evidence capture, defect reporting.“We release and hope.” / “Customers find our bugs.”Manual QA, Junior QA
    Web application testingFunctional, usability, session, form and navigation testing across supported browsers and viewports.“The site breaks on some phones/browsers.”Manual QA, Automation QA
    Mobile application testingAndroid/iOS functional testing on real devices and emulators; OS-version, interruption and network-condition testing.“The app crashes on certain devices.”Manual QA, Automation QA
    Desktop application testingInstaller, upgrade, UI, file-handling and OS-compatibility testing for Windows/macOS/Linux applications.“Our installer fails on some PCs.”Manual QA
    API testingRequest/response, status-code, authentication, schema and negative testing; contract checks.“Integrations fail in production.”API Tester
    Database testingData integrity, migration, constraints, transactions and report-query validation on test data only.“Numbers in reports do not match.”Manual QA, API Tester
    Functional testingVerification of each requirement and user story against acceptance criteria.“Does it do what we specified?”Manual QA
    Regression testingRepeatable suites (manual + automated) proving existing behaviour survives change.“Every release breaks something old.”Manual QA, Automation QA
    Integration testingData exchange, interface contracts, error handling and dependency behaviour between modules/systems.“It works alone but not together.”API Tester, Automation QA
    End-to-end testingBusiness-critical journeys across UI, API, data and third-party services.“Checkout/booking/payroll must never fail.”Automation QA
    Cross-browser testingChromium, Firefox, WebKit and agreed real-browser/OS matrix.“Looks fine on my machine.”Manual QA, Automation QA

    Accessibility testingWCAG-based automated scans plus manual keyboard and screen-reader checks.“We must meet accessibility requirements.”Manual QA, Automation QA
    Test automationPlaywright/Selenium/Cypress UI suites, pytest/Postman API suites, CI integration, reporting.“Regression takes a week by hand.”Automation QA
    Release validationEntry/exit criteria checks, QA sign-off, risk summary, production smoke test.“Can we ship on Friday?”QA Lead, Release Coordinator

    Security testing boundary

    We perform authorised assessment activity only and coordinate it with qualified security personnel (client security team or a certified penetration-testing partner). Testers may run agreed, non-destructive checks (for example verifying that an API rejects a missing token, or that error pages do not leak stack traces) and must escalate anything that looks like a vulnerability. We do not run exploit tools, brute-force, denial-of-service or scanning against systems without a signed scope, written authorisation and a named security coordinator.

    Wording we use with clients

    “Quality assurance support”, “evidence-based release recommendation”, “risk summary”. We never certify a product as defect-free, compliant or secure, and we never guarantee that a release will have no production incidents. Certification and compliance attestation are performed by authorised auditors.

    Access checklist

    • Company e-mail and calendar working; two-factor authentication enabled.
    • GitHub account added to the company organisation with the QA-Trainee team role (read on client repos, write only to the learning repository).
    • Issue tracker (Jira or equivalent) account; can open the QA-TRAINING project.

    3. First Manual-Testing Assignment (A0)

    Test the VEL Practice Shop registration and login flow against a written specification, produce a traceable test suite, execute it, log defects and report results. Time-box: 4 working days.

    Why this assignment first

    It exercises the whole manual-testing chain in miniature: read a requirement, design cases, run them, capture evidence, report a defect, and summarise status. Every later project repeats this chain with more scale or more tooling.

    Specification under test

    IDRequirement
    REQ-001Registration: Full name is required, 2–40 characters after trimming spaces.
    REQ-002Registration: Email is required and must be a valid address (name@domain.tld).
    REQ-003Registration: Age is required, a whole number from 18 to 60 inclusive.
    REQ-004Registration: Password 8–20 characters with at least one digit and at least one uppercase letter.
    REQ-005Registration: Confirm password must match the password exactly (case-sensitive).
    REQ-006Registration: the Terms checkbox must be ticked.
    REQ-007A successful registration shows “Registration successful” and opens the login view.
    REQ-008Login with registered credentials opens the shop. Any failure shows the generic message “Invalid email or password”.
    REQ-009On the 3rd consecutive failed login the account locks for 30 seconds and the message “Account locked. Try again in 30 seconds.” is shown; attempts during the lock show the same message.
    REQ-010Shop: quantity per item is a whole number 1–10. Cart total = sum(price × quantity) shown to 2 decimals; GST 18 % shown to 2 decimals (standard rounding).
    REQ-011Session expires after 90 seconds of inactivity: “Session expired. Please log in again.” and the login view opens.
    REQ-012Logout ends the session. Using the browser Back button afterwards must not show shop content.
    REQ-013The application is usable at 360 px viewport width with no horizontal scrolling.
    REQ-014Accessibility: every input has a programmatic label; every image has alt text; all functions work by keyboard with a visible focus indicator.

    Scope

    In scopeOut of scope
    Registration view, login view, shop view (cart, quantity, totals), session timeout, logout, viewport 360 px and 1280 px, keyboard access.Performance, security exploitation, other devices, real e-mail delivery, payment. Report any security concern you notice to your buddy instead of probing it.

    DayStepsDeliverable
    11. Read REQ-001 to REQ-014 twice; list ambiguities and unanswered questions.
    2. Run the app; explore for 30 minutes without a script and note what you observe (exploratory notes).
    3. Create the requirements traceability matrix with one row per requirement.    		docs/requirements-traceability.md with all 14 rows; docs/questions.md; exploratory notes
    21. For each requirement apply equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis where it has ranges (REQ-001, 003, 004, 010).
    2. Write at least 30 test cases using the template: ID, title, requirement, preconditions, steps, test data, expected result, priority.
    3. Include positive and negative cases; at least 6 for each of REQ-003 and REQ-004.    		test-cases/functional/registration-login.csv (or tool export), 30+ cases, each linked to a REQ
    31. Execute every case on Chrome and Firefox at 1280 px; REQ-013 at 360 px.
    2. Record Pass / Fail / Blocked with evidence file names per the convention.
    3. Raise a defect (template) the moment you confirm a failure; attempt to reproduce it three times.    		Filled execution log; evidence/ files; defects/DEF-nnn.md for each defect
    41. Re-check traceability: every requirement has at least one executed case.
    2. Complete the test execution report with counts, defect list, coverage and your own risk statement.
    3. Present for 10 minutes to the QA Lead.    		docs/test-execution-report.md; review notes from the QA Lead

    Acceptance criteria and marking (100 points)

    CriterionPointsFull marks when
    Traceability15All 14 requirements appear in the matrix and each links to at least one executed case.
    Test design quality25Equivalence classes and boundaries are identified and named; cases are atomic, repeatable and have measurable expected results.
    Execution discipline20Every case has a status and evidence; results are on two browsers; REQ-013 checked at 360 px.
    Defect reports25Each defect is reproducible by someone else from the report alone; severity and priority are justified; no duplicates.
    Report and honesty15Counts reconcile (pass + fail + blocked + not run = total); risks and untested areas are stated plainly.
    Pass mark: 70 / 100

    Below 70 the trainee repeats the weakest part with feedback. The QA Lead keeps a hidden answer key of seeded defects (never shown to trainees). Finding more defects does not earn extra marks; report quality does.

    4. Level 1 — Software Testing Fundamentals

    The vocabulary and mental models every tester uses daily. Nothing in later levels makes sense without them.

    DurationAbout 2 weeks (10 working days)
    PrerequisitesNone. Basic computer use and English reading ability.
    OutcomeExplains how software is built and tested, classifies a problem correctly as error, defect or failure, writes a test case and a bug report that others can follow, and applies severity and priority sensibly.
    Exit gate20-question quiz (pass ≥ 80 %) + one reviewed test case + one reviewed bug report, demonstrated to the QA Lead.

    Software development lifecycle (SDLC) models

    ModelHow it worksWhere testing happensTester's challenge
    WaterfallPhases run once in order: requirements → design → build → test → release.Late, as one phase.Defects found late are expensive; requirements may already be outdated.
    V-modelEach development phase has a matching test level (requirements ↔ acceptance, design ↔ system, code ↔ unit).Test design starts early, execution follows each build level.Needs stable, well-written requirements.
    Agile / ScrumShort iterations (sprints) deliver small increments with continuous feedback.Continuously, inside every sprint.Little documentation; regression grows every sprint; automation becomes essential.
    DevOps / CI-CDEvery commit is built, tested and deployed through an automated pipeline.Automated gates on each commit plus exploratory testing.Fast, reliable, non-flaky automation and production monitoring.

    Software testing lifecycle (STLC)

    Requirement analysis→Test planning→Test case design→Environment setup→Execution→Defect reporting→Closure

    Each STLC phase has an entry criterion (what must be true to start) and an exit criterion (what must be true to finish). The client lifecycle later in this handbook expands STLC into 16 gated stages.

    Key distinctions every trainee must be able to explain

    PairMeaningExample
    QA vs QCQuality assurance is process-oriented and prevents defects (standards, reviews, training). Quality control is product-oriented and detects defects (testing, inspection).QA: introduce a code-review checklist. QC: run the regression suite before release.
    Verification vs validationVerification: are we building the product right (against specification)? Validation: are we building the right product (against user need)?Verification: review the spec for contradictions. Validation: let a real user try the prototype.
    Error → defect → failureA human error introduces a defect (bug) in the work product; executing it may cause a failure (observable wrong behaviour).Developer mistypes >= as > (error) → age check wrong (defect) → age 18 rejected at run time (failure).
    Test scenario vs test caseA scenario is a high-level thing to test; a test case is a precise, repeatable set of steps, data and expected results.Scenario: “Registration validates age”. Cases: ages 17, 18, 60, 61, abc, empty.

    The seven testing principles (ISTQB)

    1. Testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence.
    2. Exhaustive testing is impossible; use risk and priorities to focus effort.
    3. Early testing saves time and money (review requirements before code exists).
    4. Defects cluster: a few modules usually contain most defects.
    5. Pesticide paradox: repeating the same tests stops finding new defects; refresh them.
    6. Testing is context dependent: a medical device and a game need different testing.
    7. Absence-of-defects fallacy: a defect-free system that does not meet user needs is still a failure.

    Bug lifecycle

    New→Assigned→In progress→Fixed→Ready for retest→Retest→Closed
    StateOwnerMeaning and rule
    NewTesterReported with full template. Tester has reproduced it at least twice.
    Assigned / In progressDeveloper lead → developerTriage accepted; severity/priority agreed; fix started.
    Fixed / Ready for retestDeveloperFix merged to a named build; developer notes the build number and the area at risk.
    RetestTesterRetest on the fixed build using the original steps, then run related regression.
    ClosedTesterOriginal failure no longer occurs and no new defect introduced. Only the tester closes.
    ReopenedTesterFix did not work or regressed: attach new evidence and the build number.
    Rejected / Not a bugDeveloper or product ownerBehaviour is as specified or intended. The tester may challenge once with the requirement reference.
    DuplicateTriageLink to the master defect; keep the clearest report.
    Deferred / Won't fixProduct ownerAccepted risk; must be listed in the release risk summary. Never silently dropped.

    Severity and priority

    Severity is the technical impact of the defect. Priority is the business urgency of fixing it. The tester proposes severity; the product owner decides priority.

    SeverityDefinitionExample
    Critical (S1)System unusable, data loss/corruption, security exposure, no workaround.Payment charged twice; application crashes on start.
    Major (S2)Key function fails or gives wrong results; workaround is hard.Valid users cannot register (age 18 rejected).
    Minor (S3)Function works with deviation; an easy workaround exists.Sort order wrong on a secondary list.
    Trivial (S4)Cosmetic or wording only.Typo in a success message.
    CombinationExampleTypical decision
    High severity, high priorityCheckout fails for every customer.Fix immediately; block release.
    High severity, low priorityCrash in a feature used by one client once a year.Schedule; document the workaround.
    Low severity, high priorityCompany name misspelled on the home page before a launch.Fix before launch.
    Low severity, low priorityMisaligned icon on an admin screen.Backlog.

    Test data

    TypePurposeRule
    Valid dataPositive paths.Representative of real users but fully synthetic.
    Invalid dataNegative paths.Wrong type, wrong format, too long/short, special characters.
    Boundary dataEdges of ranges.Derived from boundary-value analysis.
    Bulk / volume dataLists, search, performance.Generated by script with a fixed seed so it is reproducible.
    Masked dataRealistic shape without real identities.Only when the client provides an approved, masked copy. Never a raw production extract.

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    1.1 Software development lifecycle
    DefinitionThe ordered set of activities used to plan, build, test, release and maintain software.
    PurposeShows where defects are cheapest to find and where QA adds value.
    SetupWhiteboard or diagram tool; the SDLC table above.
    Procedure1. Name the model your current project uses. 2. Mark where requirements, build, test, release happen. 3. Mark where QA is involved today and where it should be.
    Expected outputA one-page lifecycle diagram with QA touchpoints marked.
    VerificationBuddy confirms every phase has an input, an output and an owner.
    ErrorsTreating testing as one phase at the end; ignoring maintenance.
    Reportingjournal/l1-sdlc.md.
    AssignmentDraw the lifecycle for the Practice Shop assuming Scrum and assuming Waterfall; list three differences for the tester.
    AssessmentOral: explain why a defect found in design is cheaper than one found in production.
    1.2 Software testing lifecycle
    DefinitionSeven phases of test work from requirement analysis to closure, each with entry and exit criteria.
    PurposeMakes test work repeatable and auditable.
    SetupSTLC pills above; blank entry/exit table.
    Procedure1. For each phase write entry and exit criteria. 2. Identify the deliverable. 3. Name the approver.
    Expected outputTable of seven phases × entry, exit, deliverable, approver.
    VerificationCheck that no exit criterion is “when done”; each must be measurable.
    ErrorsVague criteria (“enough testing”); skipping closure.
    Reportingjournal/l1-stlc.md.
    AssignmentFill the table for Assignment A0.
    AssessmentQuiz question on entry versus exit criteria.
    1.3 Quality assurance vs quality control
    DefinitionQA prevents defects through process; QC finds defects in the product.
    PurposeClients buy both; confusing them leads to wrong promises.
    SetupThe comparison table above.
    Procedure1. List five activities from a software project. 2. Classify each as QA or QC. 3. Justify each.
    Expected outputA five-row classification with reasons.
    VerificationQA Lead checks each classification against the definitions.
    ErrorsCalling test execution “QA” and nothing else.
    Reportingjournal/l1-qa-qc.md.
    AssignmentClassify: code review checklist, regression run, requirements workshop, bug triage, coding standard.
    AssessmentQuiz: 3 classification questions.
    1.4 Verification vs validation
    DefinitionVerification checks conformance to specification; validation checks fitness for user need.
    PurposeA product can pass verification and still fail validation.
    SetupPractice Shop spec (REQ list).
    Procedure1. Review the spec for contradictions (verification). 2. Imagine a first-time customer using the app (validation). 3. Record one finding for each.
    Expected outputTwo findings, one per activity.
    VerificationEach finding cites a requirement ID or a user need.
    ErrorsMixing the two; validating against your own opinion.
    Reportingjournal/l1-v-and-v.md.
    AssignmentProduce one spec-review finding and one usability finding.
    AssessmentOral Q&A with the buddy.
    1.5 Bugs, defects and failures
    DefinitionError (human) → defect (in the work product) → failure (observable wrong behaviour).
    PurposeCorrect words give correct root-cause conversations.
    SetupThree small examples supplied by the trainer.
    Procedure1. For each example identify the error, defect and failure. 2. State how testing would detect it.
    Expected outputThree completed chains.
    VerificationTrainer compares with the model answer.
    ErrorsReporting the failure but guessing the defect location.
    Reportingjournal/l1-defects.md.
    AssignmentWrite a chain for the age-boundary problem in A0.
    AssessmentQuiz: 4 questions.
    1.6 Test cases
    DefinitionA documented set of preconditions, inputs, steps, expected results and postconditions to verify one condition.
    PurposeMakes testing repeatable by anyone and traceable to requirements.
    SetupTemplate from the Templates Pack; spreadsheet or test-management tool.
    Procedure1. Pick one requirement. 2. Write ID, title, preconditions, steps, data, expected result. 3. Peer-review it.
    Expected outputOne atomic, measurable test case.
    VerificationA colleague who has never seen the app can run it and reach the same verdict.
    ErrorsSeveral verifications in one case; expected result like “works correctly”.
    ReportingRepository test-cases/functional/.
    AssignmentWrite five cases for REQ-002 (email).
    AssessmentReviewed by the buddy against a 6-point checklist.
    1.7 Test scenarios
    DefinitionA high-level statement of what to test, from which several cases are derived.
    PurposeGives quick coverage overviews to managers and clients.
    SetupRequirement list.
    Procedure1. Read a requirement. 2. Write scenario titles starting with “Verify that…”. 3. Derive cases later.
    Expected outputA list of scenarios with requirement IDs.
    VerificationEach requirement has at least one scenario.
    ErrorsScenarios that are really single test cases; missing negative scenarios.
    Reportingdocs/requirements-traceability.md.
    AssignmentWrite 10 scenarios for REQ-001 to REQ-009.
    AssessmentReview by the QA Lead.
    1.8 Test plans
    DefinitionA document describing scope, approach, resources, schedule, risks and criteria for testing.
    PurposeAligns the client and the team on what will and will not be tested.
    SetupTest plan template.
    Procedure1. Define scope in/out. 2. Choose test types. 3. List environments and data. 4. Add schedule, roles, risks. 5. Set entry/exit criteria.
    Expected outputA two-page test plan for A0.
    VerificationEvery section is filled; assumptions are listed.
    ErrorsCopying a plan without adapting scope and risks.
    Reportingdocs/test-plan.md.
    AssignmentWrite the test plan for the Practice Shop registration module.
    AssessmentReviewed by the Test Manager.
    1.9 Test data
    DefinitionInputs and preconditions' data used by test cases.
    PurposeWrong data gives wrong results and can break privacy rules.
    SetupSynthetic data generators or hand-written CSV.
    Procedure1. Classify data needed per case. 2. Create synthetic records. 3. Record where each record is used.
    Expected outputtest-data/ file with documented purpose per row.
    VerificationNo real personal data present; boundary values included.
    ErrorsRe-using one account for all cases; using real e-mail addresses.
    Reportingtest-data/README.md.
    AssignmentCreate 15 registration data rows including boundaries.
    AssessmentReviewed for privacy and coverage.
    1.10 Bug lifecycle
    DefinitionThe states a defect passes through from discovery to closure.
    PurposeShared understanding prevents lost or silently closed defects.
    SetupIssue tracker workflow.
    Procedure1. Create a defect. 2. Move it through assigned → fixed → retest → closed in a sandbox project. 3. Reopen one with new evidence.
    Expected outputA defect that has visited every state.
    VerificationHistory log shows who changed what and when.
    ErrorsClosing your own fix without retest; skipping the build number.
    ReportingIssue tracker history.
    AssignmentRun a lifecycle simulation with your buddy playing the developer.
    AssessmentQuiz on states and ownership.
    1.11 Severity and priority
    DefinitionSeverity = technical impact; priority = urgency to fix.
    PurposeDrives fix order and release decisions.
    SetupSeverity table above.
    Procedure1. Take five sample defects. 2. Assign severity. 3. Propose priority with business reasoning.
    Expected outputFive rows with justification.
    VerificationQA Lead agrees or explains differences.
    ErrorsUsing “critical” for every bug; mixing severity and priority.
    ReportingEach defect report.
    AssignmentRate the seven defects found in your A0 run.
    AssessmentQuiz: 4 scenarios, choose and defend.
    Level 1 exit gate

    Quiz ≥ 80 %, one test case and one bug report reviewed without major comments, and the trainee can explain the Golden Rules. Sign-off: QA Lead.

    5. Level 2 — Manual Testing

    How to analyse requirements, design effective test cases with proven techniques, execute them with evidence, and run the standard test types: smoke, sanity, regression, exploratory and UAT.

    DurationAbout 3 weeks
    PrerequisitesLevel 1 passed.
    OutcomeDesigns boundary and equivalence tests, performs exploratory sessions with a charter, runs smoke and regression cycles, and supports client acceptance testing.
    Exit gateAssignment A0 passed (≥ 70) + one exploratory-session report + technique quiz (≥ 80 %).

    Requirement analysis

    A requirement is testable when two people can independently decide whether a product meets it. Review every requirement with the checklist below and raise questions before writing test cases.

    CheckQuestion to askRed-flag words / signs
    ClearCan it be read only one way?“fast”, “user-friendly”, “etc.”, “as appropriate”, “flexible”
    MeasurableIs there a number, a limit or an observable outcome?No limits for fields, times, quantities
    CompleteAre error and boundary behaviours stated?Only the happy path described
    ConsistentDoes it contradict another requirement?Two different limits for the same field
    Feasible & traceableCan it be tested in our environment and given an ID?Needs production access; no requirement ID

    Equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis

    Equivalence partitioning (EP) divides inputs into classes that the system should treat the same way; test one value from each class. Boundary-value analysis (BVA) adds tests at the edges of each valid class, where off-by-one defects live.

    Worked example: Age field, valid 18 to 60 inclusive (REQ-003)

    PartitionClassSample valueExpected
    P1Below range (invalid)10Rejected with age message
    P2Valid range35Accepted
    P3Above range (invalid)75Rejected with age message
    P4Non-numericabcRejected
    P5Empty(blank)Rejected: required
    P6Decimal25.5Rejected: whole numbers only
    P7Negative-5Rejected
    BoundaryValueValid?Reason
    Lower − 117NoJust below the minimum
    Lower18YesMinimum, inclusive
    Lower + 119YesJust inside
    Upper − 159YesJust inside
    Upper60YesMaximum, inclusive
    Upper + 161NoJust above the maximum
    Rule of thumb

    Two-value BVA tests each edge and its nearest invalid neighbour (17, 18, 60, 61). Three-value BVA adds the nearest inside neighbours (19, 59). Use three-value BVA for money, health and safety fields.

    Second example: Password length 8–20 (REQ-004)

    LengthValid?Note
    7NoLower − 1
    8Yes (if one digit + one uppercase)Lower boundary
    20YesUpper boundary
    21NoUpper + 1
    8, no digit / no uppercaseNoRule combinations are separate cases

    Other design techniques you must recognise

    TechniqueUse it whenMini example
    Decision tableSeveral conditions combine to give an outcome.Discount: member? × order ≥ ₹1000? → 4 combinations, 4 expected discounts.
    State transitionBehaviour depends on history.Login lock-out: 0 failures → 1 → 2 → 3 (locked, 30 s) → unlock.
    Use-case / user journeyEnd-to-end flows matter.Register → login → add to cart → logout.
    Error guessingExperience tells you where bugs hide.Spaces only in name; emoji; very long text; double-click on submit.
    Pairwise (combinatorial)Many parameters with several values.Browser × OS × language reduced from 27 to ~9 cases.

    Exploratory testing

    Simultaneous learning, test design and execution, guided by a charter and time-boxed (typically 60–90 minutes). Record notes as you go; exploratory testing is not “random clicking”.

    exploratory-session-sheet.txt
    CHARTER:   Explore the Register view with unusual inputs to discover validation gaps
AREAS:     Registration form (name, email, age, passwords, terms)
TIME-BOX:  60 minutes          TESTER: <name>          BUILD: <version>
HEURISTICS: boundaries, special characters, copy/paste, double submit, keyboard only, resize window
NOTES:     (timestamped observations)
BUGS:      DEF-0xx, DEF-0xx          ISSUES/QUESTIONS: ...
DEBRIEF:   % on setup / test design / bug investigation; what to test next

    Smoke, sanity, regression and UAT compared

    TypeQuestion it answersScopeWhenWho
    SmokeIs the build stable enough to test at all?Broad and shallow: critical paths only (10–30 min).Every new build / after deploymentQA or automated pipeline
    SanityDoes the specific fix/change work and nothing obvious broke around it?Narrow and deep, unscripted or short script.After a fix or small changeQA
    RegressionDid the change break existing behaviour?Selected or full suite of previously passing tests.Before every releaseQA + automation
    UATDoes it meet business needs in real conditions?Business scenarios in a production-like environment.After QA exit, before go-liveClient users; QA supports
    Regression selection rule

    Run the full suite when risk is high or the change is wide. Otherwise run: (1) tests for changed areas, (2) tests for areas that integrate with them, (3) all critical-path tests, (4) a rotating sample of the rest. Record why anything was skipped.

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    2.1 Requirement analysis
    DefinitionReviewing requirements for clarity, completeness, consistency and testability before designing tests.
    PurposeCheapest defect prevention: ambiguity found now costs nothing.
    SetupSpec or user stories; the checklist table above.
    Procedure1. Read twice. 2. Mark ambiguous or untestable statements. 3. Write questions. 4. Create the traceability rows.
    Expected outputquestions.md + traceability matrix skeleton.
    VerificationEvery requirement has an ID, a testability verdict and an owner for open questions.
    ErrorsAssuming unstated behaviour; writing tests for requirements you do not understand.
    Reportingdocs/requirements-traceability.md.
    AssignmentAnalyse REQ-001 to REQ-014 and list at least 6 questions.
    AssessmentQA Lead reviews questions for quality, not quantity.
    2.2 Test case writing
    DefinitionProducing atomic, repeatable cases with measurable expected results.
    PurposeQuality of cases decides quality of testing.
    SetupTest case template, test data file.
    Procedure1. One case = one verification. 2. State preconditions. 3. Number the steps. 4. Write an observable expected result. 5. Link requirement and priority.
    Expected outputA suite of 30+ cases.
    VerificationA peer executes five random cases without asking questions.
    ErrorsSteps that assume knowledge (“log in normally”); duplicate cases.
    Reportingtest-cases/functional/.
    AssignmentDeliver A0 test suite.
    Assessment6-point checklist: atomic, ID, precondition, data, measurable, traceable.
    2.3 Positive and negative testing
    DefinitionPositive tests use valid input to confirm correct behaviour; negative tests use invalid input to confirm safe rejection.
    PurposeProduction users make mistakes; the system must fail safely.
    SetupEquivalence classes from each requirement.
    Procedure1. List valid classes. 2. List invalid classes. 3. Write at least one case per class. 4. Check error messages are clear and do not leak internals.
    Expected outputBalanced suite (roughly 40 % positive, 60 % negative is typical).
    VerificationEach field has both types; messages checked.
    ErrorsOnly testing the happy path.
    ReportingCase suite, tagged positive/negative.
    AssignmentFor REQ-004 write 8 positive/negative cases.
    AssessmentReview ratio and message clarity.
    2.4 Boundary-value analysis
    DefinitionTesting at and next to the edges of valid ranges.
    PurposeOff-by-one defects are among the most common.
    SetupRange limits from the spec.
    Procedure1. Identify min/max. 2. Compute min−1, min, min+1, max−1, max, max+1. 3. Add them as cases.
    Expected outputA boundary table per ranged field.
    VerificationValues computed correctly (including inclusive/exclusive wording).
    ErrorsMisreading “up to 60” as exclusive; skipping upper bounds.
    ReportingBoundary table in the test-case file.
    AssignmentProduce tables for REQ-001, 003, 004, 010.
    AssessmentQuiz: compute boundaries for 5 rules.
    2.5 Equivalence partitioning
    DefinitionGrouping inputs into classes treated identically; one representative per class.
    PurposeReduces test count without losing coverage.
    SetupInput domain per field.
    Procedure1. Split the domain into valid and invalid classes. 2. Choose one value per class. 3. Record class names.
    Expected outputA partition table.
    VerificationClasses are disjoint and cover the whole domain.
    ErrorsOverlapping classes; missing “empty” or “wrong type” classes.
    ReportingPartition table in the suite.
    AssignmentPartition the email field.
    AssessmentQuiz: 3 partitioning questions.
    2.6 Exploratory testing
    DefinitionTime-boxed, charter-driven learning and testing without pre-written steps.
    PurposeFinds defects scripts miss; covers risk quickly.
    SetupCharter sheet; screen recorder; notebook.
    Procedure1. Write the charter. 2. Test for the time-box while taking notes. 3. Log bugs immediately. 4. Debrief.
    Expected outputSession sheet with notes, bugs and next steps.
    VerificationNotes are detailed enough to reproduce each finding.
    ErrorsNo notes; wandering off charter; no time-box.
    Reportingevidence/exploratory/ + defects.
    AssignmentRun one 60-minute session on the Shop view.
    AssessmentDebrief with the QA Lead.
    2.7 Regression testing
    DefinitionRe-running tests to confirm that changes did not break existing behaviour.
    PurposeMost production incidents after releases are regressions.
    SetupStable, prioritised suite; build under test.
    Procedure1. Select tests by risk and change impact. 2. Execute. 3. Compare with the baseline. 4. Log new failures as regressions.
    Expected outputRegression result summary with reasons for skips.
    VerificationCounts reconcile; every failure has a defect or an explanation.
    ErrorsRunning everything blindly; never retiring obsolete tests.
    ReportingExecution report.
    AssignmentBuild a 20-case regression pack from A0 and run it on a modified build.
    AssessmentReviewed by the Test Manager.
    2.8 Smoke testing
    DefinitionA short, broad check that the build's critical functions work.
    PurposeStops wasting time on unusable builds.
    SetupList of 10–15 critical-path checks.
    Procedure1. Deploy build. 2. Execute checks in order. 3. Any fail → reject build.
    Expected outputPass/fail smoke verdict in under 30 minutes.
    VerificationSame checks every time, ordered by dependency.
    ErrorsSmoke suite growing into a full regression suite.
    ReportingSmoke result in the build ticket.
    AssignmentWrite the Practice Shop smoke list.
    AssessmentTimed demonstration.
    2.9 Sanity testing
    DefinitionA narrow check that a specific fix or small change works and nothing obvious nearby broke.
    PurposeQuick confidence after a fix before deeper regression.
    SetupDefect or change description.
    Procedure1. Read the fix note. 2. Retest the original steps. 3. Test two neighbouring behaviours.
    Expected outputShort verdict recorded on the defect.
    VerificationOriginal steps now pass; neighbours unaffected.
    ErrorsTreating sanity as a replacement for regression.
    ReportingDefect tracker comment.
    AssignmentRetest three fixed defects.
    AssessmentBuddy checks retest evidence.
    2.10 User acceptance testing (UAT)
    DefinitionBusiness users confirm the system meets their needs in a production-like environment.
    PurposeFinal validation and contractual acceptance.
    SetupUAT plan, scripts, accounts, test data, UAT environment.
    Procedure1. Agree scope and entry criteria. 2. Brief users. 3. Observe, log issues. 4. Triage with the client. 5. Obtain written acceptance.
    Expected outputUAT report and signed acceptance.
    VerificationAll critical issues resolved or formally accepted.
    ErrorsLetting QA decide business acceptance; vague scripts.
    ReportingUAT report template.
    AssignmentShadow a mock UAT and write the report.
    AssessmentQA Lead reviews report.
    Level 2 exit gate

    A0 passed (≥ 70 / 100); technique quiz ≥ 80 %; one exploratory session reported; 20-case regression pack run successfully. Sign-off: QA Lead.

    6. Level 3 — Web and Mobile Testing

    Browsers, devices, forms, navigation, sessions, operating-system compatibility and accessibility: the environment-specific skills that turn generic test cases into real-world coverage.

    DurationAbout 2 weeks
    PrerequisitesLevel 2 passed.
    OutcomeBuilds a risk-based browser/device matrix, uses developer tools to investigate failures, tests forms, navigation and sessions systematically, and performs first-line accessibility checks.
    Exit gateResponsive + cross-browser test report on the Practice Shop, session-test checklist, accessibility checklist run, practical demo.

    Choosing the browser, device and OS matrix

    Never promise “all browsers”. Agree a supported matrix with the client, based on their analytics, contract and risk. A typical starting point is shown below; replace it with the client's own data.

    DimensionTypical minimumHow to decide
    Desktop browsersLatest Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari (macOS) + one previous major version where analytics show > 2 % shareClient analytics (top 90 % of sessions)
    Mobile browsersChrome on Android, Safari on iOSAnalytics; app store minimum OS
    Viewports360×800 (small phone), 768×1024 (tablet), 1280×800 (laptop), 1920×1080 (desktop)Responsive breakpoints in the CSS
    Operating systemsWindows 11, macOS current, Android (current and current−2), iOS (current and current−1)Support policy in the contract
    Real devicesAt least 1 low-end Android, 1 mid-range, 1 iPhone, 1 tabletBudget and risk; use a device cloud for the long tail

    Browser developer tools: the tester's microscope

    PanelWhat to use it forEvidence to save
    ElementsInspect DOM and CSS; check labels, alt text, lang, viewport meta; test CSS states.Screenshot of the element and computed styles
    ConsoleJavaScript errors and warnings (red entries).Copy of the message with the URL and time
    NetworkRequests, status codes, timing, payloads, caching; throttle to Slow 3G; block a request to test error handling.HAR export (remove tokens and personal data first)
    ApplicationCookies, local/session storage, service workers; check cookie flags (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) and session clearing on logout.Screenshot of storage before and after logout
    Device toolbarResponsive viewport and device emulation (an approximation, not a real device).Screenshot at each tested viewport
    Lighthouse / AccessibilityQuick audits; see Level 6.Report file attached to the test run

    Form testing checklist

    AreaCheck
    Required fieldsSubmit with each required field empty, one at a time and all together; error is next to the field, announced, and the value already typed is preserved.
    Type and formatWrong type (letters in numeric), invalid e-mail forms (a@b, a@b., spaces), leading/trailing spaces, Unicode names, emoji, very long text.
    LimitsMin/max length and range boundaries (BVA); paste a value longer than the limit.
    BehaviourEnter key submits; double-click on Submit sends one request; Tab order follows visual order; autofill and password managers work.
    MessagesPlain language, no stack traces, no leakage of internal data; same wording for credential failures (do not reveal which part was wrong).
    StateBrowser Back/Refresh after submit; form keeps or clears data as specified; success confirmation shown once.

    Navigation and session testing

    TopicWhat to verify
    Links and routesNo broken links (404); external links open as specified; deep links work when logged in and redirect to login (then back) when logged out; breadcrumbs and active menu state.
    Back / forward / refreshNo duplicate submissions; protected pages are not shown after logout when pressing Back (REQ-012).
    Session timeoutIdle expiry after the specified time; clear message; unsaved work warning where required; session cannot be revived by simply reloading.
    Concurrent sessionsSame account in two browsers: behaviour matches the specification (allowed, or older session ended).
    Cookies / storageSession identifier changes after login; removed on logout; flags set; sensitive values are not stored in local storage in clear text (report, do not exploit).
    Tabs and windowsActions in one tab are reflected (or safely rejected) in another.

    Mobile testing

    ApproachStrengthsLimitsUse for
    Real devicesTrue performance, sensors, gestures, OEM quirks.Cost, availability, setup time.Final verification, performance feel, camera/biometrics
    Emulators / simulatorsCheap, fast, many OS versions.Not exact on performance, hardware, vendor skins.Early functional testing, OS-version coverage
    Device cloudLarge device catalogue, remote access.Licence cost; network latency; data-privacy review needed.Long-tail coverage

    Mobile-specific cases: install, upgrade (data preserved), uninstall; permissions (allow, deny, revoke later); interruptions (call, notification, low battery, app switch, screen rotation); network (offline, Wi-Fi ↔ mobile data switch, slow 3G); storage full; different languages and font sizes; push notifications; deep links; app store rules.

    Accessibility testing (first-line checks)

    Accessibility follows the four POUR principles of WCAG: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust. Automated tools find only a portion of issues; manual checks are mandatory.

    CheckHowPass criterion
    Keyboard onlyUnplug the mouse; use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Esc, arrow keys.Every function reachable and operable; focus is always visible; no keyboard trap.
    Labels and namesInspect inputs/buttons; check <label for> or aria-label.Every control has an accessible name.
    Alt textInspect images.Informative images have meaningful alt; decorative alt="".
    Colour contrastDevTools contrast ratio or an accessibility checker.Text ≥ 4.5 : 1 (large text ≥ 3 : 1).
    Zoom and reflowBrowser zoom 200 %; 320 px width.No loss of content or function; no horizontal scrolling for text.
    Screen readerNVDA (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), TalkBack (Android); read a form and a table.Order, names, states and errors are announced.
    Standard to quote

    Contracts normally require WCAG 2.1 or 2.2 Level AA (published by the W3C). Confirm the exact version and level in the scope. We report conformance findings; we do not issue legal compliance certificates.

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    3.1 Browser testing
    DefinitionChecking that the application works in each supported browser and version.
    PurposeRendering and JavaScript engines differ; users are split across browsers.
    SetupSupported-browser matrix; BrowserStack-class cloud or local browsers.
    Procedure1. Fix the matrix. 2. Run smoke + top journeys per browser. 3. Compare screenshots. 4. Log browser-specific defects with version.
    Expected outputMatrix with pass/fail per journey.
    VerificationEach fail reproduced twice and checked in a second browser to confirm it is browser-specific.
    ErrorsTesting only in the developer's browser; not recording the exact version.
    ReportingCross-browser table in the execution report.
    AssignmentRun the A0 suite in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit.
    AssessmentReport reviewed by QA Lead.
    3.2 Responsive testing
    DefinitionVerifying layout and function at different viewport sizes and orientations.
    PurposeA large share of traffic is mobile.
    SetupDevTools device toolbar; real phone/tablet.
    Procedure1. Test the breakpoints and 10 px either side. 2. Rotate. 3. Check touch targets (≥ 24 px) and text zoom.
    Expected outputScreenshots per viewport; list of layout defects.
    VerificationNo horizontal scroll, no overlap, no clipped controls.
    ErrorsRelying on emulation only; ignoring landscape.
    ReportingEvidence folder per viewport.
    AssignmentTest REQ-013 at 360 px.
    AssessmentPractical review.
    3.3 Form testing
    DefinitionValidation, submission, error handling and usability of input forms.
    PurposeForms are where users and data enter the system.
    SetupForm test checklist; synthetic data.
    Procedure1. Map every field and rule. 2. Apply EP/BVA. 3. Test submission behaviours. 4. Verify messages and persistence.
    Expected outputForm test suite and results.
    VerificationEach rule has at least one passing and one failing input.
    ErrorsNot testing paste, autofill, double submit or whitespace.
    ReportingTest cases linked to requirements.
    AssignmentFull registration-form suite (A0).
    AssessmentA0 marking rubric.
    3.4 Navigation testing
    DefinitionVerifying links, menus, routing, back/forward and deep links.
    PurposeBroken navigation means lost users.
    SetupSitemap; link checker (optional).
    Procedure1. Build a route map. 2. Click every route. 3. Test logged-in/out access. 4. Test Back/forward/refresh.
    Expected outputRoute map with verdicts.
    VerificationNo 404s; protected routes redirect correctly.
    ErrorsSkipping footer and error pages.
    ReportingRoute table.
    AssignmentMap and test all routes of the Practice Shop.
    AssessmentDemonstration.
    3.5 Session testing
    DefinitionVerifying login state, timeout, logout and concurrent-session behaviour.
    PurposeSession faults cause data exposure and lost work.
    SetupTwo browsers; DevTools Application panel.
    Procedure1. Log in. 2. Stay idle until timeout. 3. Log out and use Back. 4. Open second session. 5. Compare with REQ-011/012.
    Expected outputSession checklist with evidence.
    VerificationObserved behaviour matches the spec in each step.
    ErrorsUsing a stopwatch only once; forgetting to clear storage between cases.
    ReportingChecklist + screenshots.
    AssignmentRun the session checklist.
    AssessmentQA Lead review.
    3.6 Mobile device testing
    DefinitionTesting apps and mobile websites on real or virtual devices.
    PurposeHardware, OS and network conditions change behaviour.
    SetupAndroid emulator, one real phone, cloud account if licensed.
    Procedure1. Install the build. 2. Run core journeys. 3. Run interruptions and network cases. 4. Record device/OS.
    Expected outputDevice-by-journey results.
    VerificationEvery failure notes device model, OS version, build.
    ErrorsNot recording the OS version; testing only on a flagship phone.
    ReportingExecution report.
    AssignmentTest the Practice Shop on a phone browser.
    AssessmentPractical review.
    3.7 Operating-system compatibility
    DefinitionConfirming the product works across supported OS versions and configurations.
    PurposeOS updates frequently break software.
    SetupVMs or test machines; compatibility matrix.
    Procedure1. List supported OS versions. 2. Install/run smoke. 3. Test upgrade from previous version.
    Expected outputCompatibility matrix.
    VerificationInstall, run, upgrade and uninstall pass on each OS.
    ErrorsSkipping upgrade and uninstall paths.
    ReportingMatrix document.
    AssignmentBuild a matrix for a desktop app of your choice.
    AssessmentReviewed by the QA Lead.
    3.8 Accessibility testing
    DefinitionChecking that people with disabilities can use the product.
    PurposeLegal duty, ethical duty and a bigger market.
    SetupKeyboard, NVDA/VoiceOver, axe DevTools, Lighthouse.
    Procedure1. Keyboard walk-through. 2. Automated scan. 3. Screen-reader read. 4. Zoom/contrast checks. 5. Log issues with WCAG criterion.
    Expected outputAccessibility findings list with WCAG references.
    VerificationEvery automated finding triaged; manual checks documented.
    ErrorsTrusting automated scores alone.
    ReportingFindings in the defect tracker with the a11y label.
    AssignmentAudit the registration page.
    AssessmentAssessment by the QA Lead.
    Level 3 exit gate

    Cross-browser/responsive report, session checklist and accessibility findings for the Practice Shop reviewed and approved. Sign-off: QA Lead.

    7. Level 4 — API Testing

    Testing the interface behind the screen: HTTP, authentication, JSON, schemas, negative cases, and the foundations of API automation.

    DurationAbout 2 weeks
    PrerequisitesLevel 3 passed. Basic JSON understanding.
    OutcomeSends and validates requests with curl and Postman, designs positive and negative API cases, validates JSON against a schema, and reports API defects with request/response evidence.
    Exit gatePractice API test collection with ≥ 40 requests, ≥ 8 defects correctly reported, schema validation demonstrated.

    HTTP methods

    MethodPurposeSafe?Idempotent?Typical success
    GETRead a resource.YesYes200
    POSTCreate a resource or trigger an action.NoNo201 (+ Location), 200, 202
    PUTReplace a resource completely.NoYes200 or 204
    PATCHPartially update a resource.NoNot guaranteed200 or 204
    DELETERemove a resource.NoYes204 (or 200)
    HEAD / OPTIONSHeaders only / allowed methods and CORS.YesYes200 / 204
    Idempotent means repeat-safe

    Repeating an idempotent request leaves the server in the same state. Test it: send the same PUT twice and check state is unchanged; send DELETE twice and check the second response is 404 (resource already gone), not another 204.

    Status codes to know by heart

    CodeMeaningWhen a test expects it
    200 OKSuccess with a body.Valid GET or update
    201 CreatedResource created; Location header gives its URL.Valid POST
    204 No ContentSuccess, no body.Valid DELETE
    400 Bad RequestMalformed or invalid input.Missing field, wrong type, bad range
    401 UnauthorizedNot authenticated (missing/invalid/expired token).No token or bad token
    403 ForbiddenAuthenticated but not allowed.Normal user calls admin endpoint
    404 Not FoundResource does not exist.Unknown id; deleted resource
    405 Method Not AllowedMethod unsupported on this URL.DELETE /api/health
    409 ConflictState conflict.Duplicate unique value
    415 / 422Unsupported media type / semantically invalid.Wrong Content-Type; business-rule failure
    429 Too Many RequestsRate limit.Burst above the limit (only if rate limiting is specified)
    500 / 502 / 503 / 504Server error / bad gateway / unavailable / gateway timeout.Never expected from client mistakes; report as defects

    Authentication types

    TypeHow it travelsWhat to test
    API keyHeader such as X-API-Key.Missing, wrong, revoked key; key never in URLs or logs.
    Basic authAuthorization: Basic base64(user:pass).Only over HTTPS; wrong credentials → 401.
    Bearer / JWTAuthorization: Bearer <token>.Missing, malformed, expired, tampered token → 401; role checks → 403.
    OAuth 2.0Access token obtained from an authorisation server.Scopes, token expiry, refresh flow, invalid grant.

    Practice API contract (the target for Projects 3 and 5)

    Method and pathAuthSuccessSpecified errors
    GET /api/healthNo200 {"status":"ok","service":"vel-practice-api"}—
    POST /api/auth/loginNo200 {token, expiresIn}400 missing field; 401 invalid credentials
    GET /api/products?page=&limit=No200 {items,page,limit,total}; limit 1–50, default 5400 invalid page/limit
    GET /api/products/{id}No200 product {id,name,price,stock}400 id not an integer; 404 unknown id
    POST /api/productsBearer201 + Location400 invalid body; 401; 409 duplicate name
    PUT /api/products/{id}Bearer200 updated product400; 401; 404
    DELETE /api/products/{id}Bearer204401; 404 unknown or already deleted
    GET /api/ordersBearer200 list401 without valid token
    GET /api/slow?delay=msNo200 after delay (0–5000 ms)400 invalid delay

    Validation rules for products: name required string 1–60 characters; price number > 0; stock integer ≥ 0. Practice credentials (synthetic, for the local server only): qa@example.test / Passw0rd!QA.

    Worked example with curl

    bash
    # 1. Health
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/health

# 2. Login and capture the token (jq optional)
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"qa@example.test","password":"Passw0rd!QA"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])')

# 3. Create a product (positive)
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Marker","price":3.5,"stock":10}'
# Expect: HTTP/1.1 201 Created  +  Location: /api/products/<id>

# 4. Negative: price must be > 0
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Free item","price":0,"stock":1}'
# Expect: 400 with an error message  (if you get 201, you have found a defect)

    JSON schema validation

    A JSON Schema states the shape of a valid response: required fields, types, ranges. Validating every response against a schema catches type drift (for example price returned as a string) that status-code checks miss.

    automation/api/schemas/product.schema.json
    {
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "Product",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "name", "price", "stock"],
  "properties": {
    "id":    { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 },
    "name":  { "type": "string", "minLength": 1, "maxLength": 60 },
    "price": { "type": "number", "exclusiveMinimum": 0 },
    "stock": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}

    API negative-testing checklist

    CategoryCases
    AuthenticationNo token; malformed token; expired token; token of another user; token in the wrong header.
    Input validationMissing required field; wrong type (string for number); null; empty string; too long; negative; zero; huge number; special characters; wrong Content-Type; invalid JSON.
    Boundarieslimit 0, 1, 50, 51; page 0, −1; price 0.01 and 0.
    Resource stateUnknown id; already-deleted id; duplicate create; update of a deleted resource.
    MethodsUnsupported method on each URL → 405 with Allow header.
    Errors and leakageNo stack traces, SQL, file paths or internal hostnames in error bodies; errors use the documented JSON shape and Content-Type.
    Performance sanityResponse time for a single request within the agreed budget; large limit does not exhaust the server.

    Postman essentials

    1. Create a Collection (Practice API) with a Collection Variable baseUrl = http://localhost:8080.
    2. Create an Environment local; store the token in a variable (secrets use secret-type variables and are never committed).
    3. Add requests per endpoint; add Tests scripts (JavaScript) to assert status, time, headers and body.
    4. Run the collection with the Collection Runner, or from CI with newman run collection.json -e local.json (Newman is Apache-2.0, registry-verified).
    5. Export collection and a sanitised environment into automation/api/postman/.
    postman-tests.js
    // Postman "Tests" tab for POST /api/products
pm.test("status is 201", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.test("Location header present", () => pm.response.to.have.header("Location"));
pm.test("response time < 500 ms", () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(500));
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.test("price is a number", () => pm.expect(body.price).to.be.a("number"));
pm.collectionVariables.set("createdId", body.id);

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    4.1 HTTP methods
    DefinitionVerbs that tell the server what operation to perform on a resource.
    PurposeWrong method use is a common API defect and a security smell.
    Setupcurl or Postman; Practice API running.
    Procedure1. Call each endpoint with each method. 2. Record status. 3. Compare with the contract.
    Expected outputA method × endpoint matrix of observed statuses.
    VerificationUnsupported methods return 405 with Allow.
    ErrorsTesting only GET and POST.
    ReportingAPI test sheet.
    AssignmentBuild the matrix for all Practice API endpoints.
    AssessmentReviewed against the contract.
    4.2 Request and response validation
    DefinitionChecking headers, status, body and timing of every call.
    PurposeTests are only as good as their assertions.
    SetupPostman Tests tab or pytest.
    Procedure1. Define the expected status, headers and body. 2. Assert each. 3. Add time budget.
    Expected outputA request with 4+ assertions.
    VerificationBreak the request on purpose; the assertion must fail.
    ErrorsOnly asserting 200.
    ReportingCollection export.
    AssignmentAdd assertions to five requests.
    AssessmentDemo.
    4.3 Status codes
    DefinitionThree-digit codes that summarise the result of a request.
    PurposeClients branch on them; wrong codes break integrations.
    SetupStatus-code table.
    Procedure1. For each endpoint list success and error codes from the contract. 2. Provoke each. 3. Compare.
    Expected outputExpected vs actual table.
    VerificationAll specified codes provoked at least once.
    ErrorsAccepting 500 as an “error response”.
    ReportingDefects for each mismatch.
    AssignmentProvoke 400, 401, 404, 409 on the Practice API.
    AssessmentQuiz: 10 codes.
    4.4 Authentication
    DefinitionProving identity to the API (key, basic, bearer/JWT, OAuth).
    PurposeBroken authentication exposes data.
    SetupPractice credentials; Postman.
    Procedure1. Call without token. 2. Wrong token. 3. Valid token. 4. Expired token (if available).
    Expected output401 for each invalid case; 200/201 for valid.
    VerificationNo protected endpoint works without a valid token.
    ErrorsSharing tokens in screenshots; committing tokens.
    ReportingDefects; security coordinator notified for access-control faults.
    AssignmentTest all protected endpoints without a token.
    AssessmentQA Lead review; escalation rule explained.
    4.5 JSON validation
    DefinitionChecking the structure and values of JSON bodies.
    PurposeBad JSON breaks clients.
    SetupBrowser/JSON viewer, Postman.
    Procedure1. Check types. 2. Check required fields. 3. Check nested objects and arrays. 4. Check ranges.
    Expected outputValidation notes per endpoint.
    VerificationMatches the documented model.
    ErrorsEyeballing instead of asserting.
    ReportingAssertions in tests.
    AssignmentValidate /products response items.
    AssessmentPractical test.
    4.6 Schema validation
    DefinitionAutomated check of a response against a JSON Schema.
    PurposeDetects silent type changes and missing fields.
    SetupSchema file; Postman tv4/Ajv or Python jsonschema (MIT, registry-verified).
    Procedure1. Write the schema. 2. Validate every product in the list. 3. Add negative schema (extra field).
    Expected outputSchema test that fails for the broken item.
    VerificationSchema catches the seeded string-price defect.
    ErrorsSchema too loose (type: object only).
    ReportingDefect with schema error message.
    AssignmentWrite schemas for Product and Product list.
    AssessmentPeer review.
    4.7 API negative testing
    DefinitionSending invalid, missing or hostile input to prove safe failure.
    PurposeReal clients and attackers send unexpected data.
    SetupNegative-testing checklist.
    Procedure1. Pick endpoint. 2. Apply each category. 3. Record actual response. 4. Raise defects for 5xx and silent acceptance.
    Expected output20+ negative cases with results.
    VerificationNo 5xx; clear 4xx; no data change on rejected requests.
    ErrorsStopping at obvious cases.
    ReportingDefect reports with request/response.
    AssignmentWrite 20 negative cases for /api/products.
    AssessmentReview.
    4.8 API automation
    DefinitionRunning API checks from code (pytest + requests) or Newman, repeatably.
    PurposeFast, stable regression for integrations.
    SetupPython 3.11+, pytest, requests, jsonschema.
    Procedure1. Create fixtures for base URL and token. 2. Write parametrised tests. 3. Run in CI. 4. Publish results.
    Expected outputPassing and failing tests with HTML/JUnit report.
    VerificationKnown defects show as expected failures (xfail with defect ID).
    ErrorsShared state between tests; hard-coded ids and secrets.
    Reportingautomation/api/ and reports.
    AssignmentAutomate 15 cases (Project 5).
    AssessmentCode review against checklist.
    Level 4 exit gate

    Collection ≥ 40 requests with assertions, ≥ 8 correctly reported API defects, schema validation demonstrated. Sign-off: QA Lead.

    8. Level 5 — Automation Testing

    Turn stable, repeatable, valuable manual tests into reliable code: Python or JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals, Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, pytest, Postman, Page Object Model, fixtures, test data and CI.

    DurationAbout 4 weeks
    PrerequisitesLevels 1–4 passed. Comfortable using a terminal and Git.
    OutcomeWrites maintainable UI and API automation with a Page Object Model and fixtures, runs it locally and in CI, and reports automation coverage honestly.
    Exit gateAutomated suite (≥ 15 UI + ≥ 15 API tests) running green in GitHub Actions with a published report; code review passed.

    What to automate (and what not to)

    AutomateDo not automate (yet)
    Stable features with clear expected results · smoke and regression paths · data-driven checks (many inputs, same steps) · API contract and schema checks · tests run on every build · tests too tedious or error-prone by hand.Features still changing daily · one-off checks · exploratory testing and usability judgement · visual design opinions · tests that need physical hardware you cannot control · anything whose expected result you cannot state precisely.
    Automation return-on-investment rule

    Automate when (manual minutes per run × number of runs) is greater than (build time + maintenance time). Example: a 30-minute manual regression run 40 times a year = 20 hours. If automating costs 16 hours and maintenance 4 hours/year, break-even is in the first year; with 6 runs a year it never pays back.

    The test pyramid

    LayerShareSpeedExamples
    Unit (developers)Many (≈ 70 %)MillisecondsFunction tests, mocked dependencies
    API / integration (QA + dev)Some (≈ 20 %)SecondsContract, schema, auth, error handling
    UI end-to-end (QA)Few (≈ 10 %)Tens of secondsCritical journeys: register → login → buy

    QA owns the top two layers. The more logic you can verify at API level, the faster and less flaky the suite.

    Choosing a UI automation tool

    ToolLanguagesBrowsersStrengthsLimitationsLicence (registry-verified 2026-11-04)
    PlaywrightTypeScript/JS, Python, Java, .NETChromium, Firefox, WebKitAuto-waiting, tracing, parallel, API testing, codegenWebKit ≠ real Safari; no real mobile devices (emulation)Apache-2.0 (v1.64.1)
    Selenium WebDriverJava, Python, C#, JS, RubyAll major via driversStandard, huge ecosystem, GridMore boilerplate, manual waits, slowerApache-2.0 (v4.52.0)
    CypressJavaScript/TypeScriptChromium, Firefox, WebKit (experimental)Great developer experience, time-travel debuggingSingle-origin history, no multi-tab; paid cloud featuresMIT (v16.2.1); Cypress Cloud is a paid service

    Selection rule: default to Playwright for new projects; use Selenium when the client already owns a Selenium Grid or needs a language or browser Playwright lacks; use Cypress when the client team is JavaScript-only and wants developers to write tests too. Alternatives to know: WebdriverIO (MIT), Appium for native mobile (Apache-2.0), Robot Framework.

    Python fundamentals required (one-page primer)

    python-primer.py
    # Variables, collections, f-strings
user = {"email": "qa@example.test", "age": 18}
ages = [17, 18, 60, 61]
print(f"{user['email']} has age {user['age']}")

# Functions and loops
def is_valid_age(age: int) -> bool:
    return 18 <= age <= 60          # the spec: inclusive range

for a in ages:
    print(a, is_valid_age(a))       # False True True False

# Exceptions and files
import json, pathlib
try:
    data = json.loads(pathlib.Path("test-data/users.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
except FileNotFoundError:
    data = []

    JavaScript/TypeScript equivalent topics: const/let, arrow functions, arrays/objects, async/await, modules (import), try/catch, JSON. Teach one language first; the second takes days, not weeks.

    pytest essentials

    ConceptUseExample
    Test discoveryFiles test_*.py, functions test_*.pytest -q
    FixturesReusable setup/teardown with scopes (function, module, session).@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
    ParametrisationOne test, many data rows.@pytest.mark.parametrize("age,ok", [(17,False),(18,True)])
    MarkersSelect groups; mark known defects.-m smoke; @pytest.mark.xfail(reason="DEF-001", strict=True)
    conftest.pyShared fixtures per directory.base URL, auth token, browser page
    ReportsJUnit XML for CI; HTML via pytest-html (MPL-2.0).--junitxml=reports/junit.xml

    Playwright (Python) with Page Object Model and fixtures

    The code below is the real starter code from qa-project-template/ (it is embedded from the repository when this handbook is built, so it cannot drift). Install and run (Playwright downloads its browsers once):

    bash
    cd qa-project-template
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r automation/requirements.txt
playwright install chromium firefox
export QA_EMAIL=qa@example.test QA_PASSWORD='<see practice-api/README.md>'
pytest -m smoke                 # critical path only
pytest automation/ui --browser chromium --browser firefox
    automation/page-objects/register_page.py
    """Page object: Register view of the VEL Practice Shop. Locators and actions only; assertions belong in the tests."""
from playwright.sync_api import Page


class RegisterPage:
    def __init__(self, page: Page, url: str):
        self.page, self.url = page, url
        self.name = page.get_by_label("Full name")
        self.email = page.get_by_label("Email")
        self.age = page.get_by_label("Age")
        self.password = page.get_by_label("Password", exact=True)
        self.confirm = page.get_by_label("Confirm password")
        self.terms = page.get_by_label("I accept the terms")
        self.submit_btn = page.get_by_role("button", name="Register")
        self.alerts = page.get_by_role("alert")

    def open(self) -> "RegisterPage":
        self.page.goto(f"{self.url}#/register")
        return self

    def register(self, name="Asha Rao", email="qa@example.test", age=35, password="Passw0rdOK", confirm=None, terms=True):
        self.name.fill(name)
        self.email.fill(email)
        self.age.fill(str(age))
        self.password.fill(password)
        self.confirm.fill(password if confirm is None else confirm)
        if terms:
            self.terms.check()
        self.submit_btn.click()
    automation/ui/test_registration.py
    """Starter UI tests (Project 4 starts here). Extend them: boundaries, negative cases, login, shop, session, responsive, accessibility."""
import pytest
from markers import known
from playwright.sync_api import expect
from test_data import unique_email


@pytest.mark.smoke
def test_valid_registration_succeeds(register_page, login_page):
    register_page.open().register("Asha Rao", unique_email(), 35, "Passw0rdOK")
    expect(login_page.status).to_contain_text("Registration successful")            # REQ-007


@pytest.mark.parametrize("age", [17, "abc", "", "25.5", pytest.param(61, marks=known("DEF-002: age 61 accepted although REQ-003 maximum is 60"))])
def test_invalid_age_is_rejected(register_page, age):                                # REQ-003: invalid classes + neighbours of the boundaries
    register_page.open().register("Asha Rao", unique_email(), age, "Passw0rdOK")
    expect(register_page.alerts.first).to_be_visible()


@known("DEF-001: age 18 rejected although REQ-003 allows 18-60 inclusive")
def test_age_lower_boundary_18_accepted(register_page, login_page):
    register_page.open().register("Asha Rao", unique_email(), 18, "Passw0rdOK")
    expect(login_page.status).to_contain_text("Registration successful")
    automation/ui/conftest.py
    """UI fixtures. Environment: BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8000), BUILD (1.0 or 1.1)."""
import os

import pytest
from login_page import LoginPage
from register_page import RegisterPage
from shop_page import ShopPage
from test_data import valid_user

BASE = os.getenv("BASE_URL", "http://localhost:8000").rstrip("/")
BUILD = os.getenv("BUILD", "1.0")


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def browser_type_launch_args(browser_type_launch_args):
    """Optional: point Playwright at an existing Chromium/Chrome (CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE) when `playwright install` is not possible."""
    exe = os.getenv("CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE")
    return {**browser_type_launch_args, **({"executable_path": exe} if exe else {})}


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def build() -> str:
    return BUILD


@pytest.fixture
def app_url() -> str:
    return f"{BASE}/?build={BUILD}"


@pytest.fixture
def register_page(page, app_url):
    return RegisterPage(page, app_url)


@pytest.fixture
def login_page(page, app_url):
    return LoginPage(page, app_url)


@pytest.fixture
def registered_user(page, app_url) -> dict:
    """Register a fresh synthetic user through the UI (each test has its own browser context, so its own storage)."""
    user = valid_user()
    reg = RegisterPage(page, app_url).open()
    reg.register(**user)
    LoginPage(page, app_url).status.wait_for()
    return user


@pytest.fixture
def shop(page, app_url, registered_user) -> ShopPage:
    login = LoginPage(page, app_url)
    login.login(registered_user["email"], registered_user["password"])
    page.get_by_role("heading", name="Welcome", exact=False).wait_for()
    return ShopPage(page, app_url)
    pytest.ini
    [pytest]
testpaths = automation
pythonpath = automation/page-objects automation/fixtures
addopts = -ra --strict-markers
markers =
    smoke: critical-path checks (run on every build)
    regression: full regression pack
    api: API tests
    ui: browser tests
    a11y: accessibility checks
    Why `xfail(strict=True)`

    A known defect appears as an expected failure linked to its defect ID. When developers fix it, the test suddenly passes and strict=True turns that into a failure, forcing you to remove the marker and close the defect. The suite stays green yet honest. Never hide an unexplained failure behind xfail.

    Selenium and Cypress at a glance

    selenium-example.py
    # Selenium (Python) - explicit wait, never time.sleep
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

driver = webdriver.Chrome()
try:
    driver.get("http://localhost:8000/#/login")
    WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "login-email")))
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "login-email").send_keys("nobody@example.test")
finally:
    driver.quit()
    cypress-example.cy.js
    // Cypress (JavaScript) - retries assertions automatically
describe('Login view', () => {
  it('shows a generic message for a wrong password', () => {
    cy.visit('http://localhost:8000/#/login');
    cy.get('#login-email').type('qa@example.test');
    cy.get('#login-password').type('wrong-password');
    cy.contains('button', 'Log in').click();
    cy.get('[role=alert]').should('contain.text', 'Invalid email or password');
  });
});

    Page Object Model, fixtures and test data: the rules

    TopicRules
    Page Object ModelOne class per page/component. Locators and actions live in the page object; assertions live in the test. Prefer role/label locators (get_by_role, get_by_label) over CSS/XPath; never use positional XPath such as //div[3]/span[2].
    WaitingNever sleep. Use auto-waiting actions and web-first assertions (expect(locator).to_be_visible()).
    IndependenceEach test creates its own data and can run alone, in any order, in parallel.
    FixturesUse fixtures for browser context, base URL, authenticated session, API client; put clean-up after yield.
    Test dataSynthetic only; unique values (uuid) for anything that must be unique; data files in test-data/ with a README; no secrets in code — read from environment variables or the CI secret store.
    ReportingJUnit XML + HTML report + traces/screenshots on failure, uploaded as CI artifacts.

    Continuous integration with GitHub Actions

    .github/workflows/qa.yml
    # QA pipeline: starts the local practice targets, runs API + UI tests, uploads reports.
# Required repository secret: QA_PASSWORD (the practice API password). Never write credentials in this file.
name: QA
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 2 * * 1-5"        # nightly regression on weekdays (UTC)
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  api-and-ui:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    env:
      QA_EMAIL: qa@example.test            # synthetic practice user (not a secret)
      QA_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.QA_PASSWORD }}
      PRACTICE_API_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.QA_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: automation/requirements.txt
      - run: pip install -r automation/requirements.txt
      - run: playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Start practice targets
        run: |
          python3 practice-api/server.py --port 8080 &
          python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory practice-app &
          sleep 2
          curl --fail --silent http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/health
      - name: Run tests
        run: pytest automation -q --junitxml=automation/reports/junit.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: qa-reports
          path: automation/reports

    Pin actions to a major version tag at minimum (a full commit SHA is stricter). Keep secrets in GitHub Actions secrets, never in the YAML. Free-tier minutes and runner limits change: check the current GitHub Actions documentation before promising a client a CI budget.

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    5.1 Python or JavaScript/TypeScript fundamentals
    DefinitionThe programming basics needed to read and write test code.
    PurposeAutomation is software development; weak code makes flaky tests.
    SetupPython 3.11+ or Node LTS; VS Code.
    Procedure1. Work through variables, functions, loops, collections, files, exceptions. 2. Solve 10 exercises. 3. Write a script that reads CSV test data.
    Expected outputScript that prints a pass/fail table from a CSV.
    VerificationRuns on a clean machine with one command.
    ErrorsCopy-pasting code you cannot explain.
    Reportingjournal/l5-programming.md.
    AssignmentImplement is_valid_age and test it with all BVA values.
    AssessmentCoding quiz + code walk-through.
    5.2 Playwright
    DefinitionA framework that drives Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with auto-waiting and tracing.
    PurposeFast, reliable cross-browser UI automation.
    Setuppip install pytest-playwright (or npm init playwright), playwright install.
    Procedure1. Record with codegen to learn locators. 2. Rewrite as page objects. 3. Add assertions. 4. Run headed, then headless.
    Expected outputGreen tests plus trace viewer on a failure.
    VerificationRun 5 times; zero flakiness.
    ErrorsFixed sleeps; brittle CSS selectors.
    ReportingHTML/JUnit report; trace zip.
    AssignmentAutomate the A0 smoke list.
    AssessmentCode review.
    5.3 Selenium
    DefinitionThe long-standing WebDriver standard for browser automation.
    PurposeMany clients already run Selenium Grid.
    Setuppip install selenium; Selenium Manager fetches drivers.
    Procedure1. Open a page. 2. Use explicit waits. 3. Interact. 4. Always quit().
    Expected outputA passing login-failure test.
    VerificationNo time.sleep in the code.
    ErrorsStale-element errors; implicit + explicit wait mixing.
    ReportingSame report format.
    AssignmentPort one Playwright test to Selenium and compare effort.
    AssessmentShort comparison write-up.
    5.4 Cypress
    DefinitionA JavaScript test runner that executes inside the browser.
    PurposeDeveloper-friendly tests for JS teams.
    SetupNode LTS; npm i -D cypress.
    Procedure1. npx cypress open. 2. Write a spec. 3. Use cy.intercept to stub a network call.
    Expected outputPassing spec with video/screenshots.
    VerificationBreak the app; test fails with a clear message.
    ErrorsTrying multi-tab/multi-origin flows; async/await misuse.
    ReportingCypress run output + artifacts.
    AssignmentWrite 3 specs for the login view.
