    AssessmentReview.
    5.5 pytest
    DefinitionThe standard Python test framework with fixtures and parametrisation.
    PurposeClean, scalable test suites with rich plugins.
    Setuppip install pytest; folder automation/.
    Procedure1. Write tests. 2. Add fixtures. 3. Parametrise BVA data. 4. Add markers (smoke, regression).
    Expected outputSuite selectable by marker.
    Verificationpytest -m smoke runs only smoke tests.
    ErrorsOver-complicated fixtures; shared mutable state.
    ReportingJUnit XML.
    AssignmentConvert 10 boundary cases to a parametrised test.
    AssessmentReview.
    5.6 Postman
    DefinitionA GUI and runner for building, testing and documenting API requests.
    PurposeFastest way to explore and regress-test an API.
    SetupPostman app (proprietary, free tier); Newman CLI (Apache-2.0).
    Procedure1. Build a collection. 2. Add tests. 3. Use environments. 4. Run with Newman.
    Expected outputCollection + environment files; Newman run output.
    VerificationNewman exits non-zero when a test fails.
    ErrorsSecrets stored in exported files.
    ReportingNewman JUnit report.
    AssignmentAutomate Level-4 collection through Newman.
    AssessmentDemonstration.
    5.7 API automation
    DefinitionCode-driven API tests with pytest and requests.
    PurposeStable, fast regression and contract checks.
    Setuppip install requests jsonschema pytest.
    Procedure1. Fixtures for base URL, token. 2. Test positive and negative cases. 3. Validate schema. 4. Mark known defects xfail.
    Expected output15+ API tests including schema checks.
    VerificationSeeded API defects appear as strict xfail.
    ErrorsHard-coded ids; test order dependence.
    ReportingJUnit report.
    AssignmentProject 5.
    AssessmentCode review.
    5.8 Page Object Model
    DefinitionA pattern that wraps each page's locators and actions in a class.
    PurposeOne change in the UI means one change in the code.
    SetupExisting UI tests.
    Procedure1. Identify repeated locators. 2. Move them into a class. 3. Keep assertions in tests.
    Expected outputRefactored suite with page objects.
    VerificationTests still pass; duplicated locators removed.
    ErrorsPage objects that contain assertions and business rules.
    ReportingCommit message refactor(ui): introduce RegisterPage.
    AssignmentRefactor your Playwright tests.
    AssessmentReview.
    5.9 Fixtures
    DefinitionReusable setup and teardown code injected into tests.
    PurposeRemoves duplication and guarantees clean state.
    Setuppytest fixtures.
    Procedure1. Create session, module and function fixtures. 2. Use yield for cleanup. 3. Compose fixtures.
    Expected outputconftest.py with documented fixtures.
    VerificationTests pass in any order and in parallel (pytest -p xdist -n 2).
    ErrorsGlobal state; hidden dependencies.
    ReportingDocstrings on fixtures.
    AssignmentWrite an authenticated-API fixture.
    AssessmentReview.
    5.10 Test data management
    DefinitionCreating, storing and cleaning the data that tests use.
    PurposeMost flaky tests are data problems.
    Setuptest-data/, factories, API seeding.
    Procedure1. Generate unique data. 2. Seed via API where possible. 3. Clean up. 4. Document datasets.
    Expected outputData strategy page and factory helpers.
    VerificationTwo parallel runs do not collide.
    ErrorsShared accounts; real data.
    Reportingtest-data/README.md.
    AssignmentWrite a user factory with unique e-mails.
    AssessmentReview.
    5.11 CI integration
    DefinitionRunning tests automatically on every change in a pipeline.
    PurposeFast feedback; protects the main branch.
    SetupGitHub repository, Actions workflow, secrets.
    Procedure1. Add workflow. 2. Cache dependencies. 3. Upload reports. 4. Make the check required on pull requests.
    Expected outputGreen workflow run with artifacts.
    VerificationBreak a test on a branch; the check fails.
    ErrorsSecrets in YAML; tests depending on a developer's machine.
    ReportingLink to workflow run in the QA report.
    AssignmentCommit the workflow and show a failing and a passing run.
    AssessmentReview.
    Level 5 exit gate

    ≥ 15 UI + ≥ 15 API tests, green in CI with published reports, reviewed code, and an automation coverage statement that separates automated, manual-only and not yet tested. Sign-off: QA Lead + Automation QA.

    9. Level 6 — Advanced QA

    Performance, load, stress and reliability testing; accessibility at scale; security-test coordination; database validation; coverage; and managing flaky tests.

    DurationAbout 4 weeks
    PrerequisitesLevels 1–5 passed.
    OutcomePlans and runs a controlled performance test with a workload model and thresholds, automates accessibility checks, validates data directly in a test database, coordinates security testing with qualified people, and keeps the automation suite trustworthy.
    Exit gateControlled performance test report + accessibility automation + database validation script + flaky-test register, all reviewed.

    Performance testing: vocabulary

    Test typeQuestionLoad shapeTypical duration
    Baseline / smokeWhat is performance with one user?1–5 virtual users (VUs)Minutes
    LoadDoes it meet targets at expected peak?Ramp to expected peak and hold20–60 min steady state
    StressWhere does it break and how does it fail?Increase until errors or saturationUntil breaking point
    SpikeCan it absorb a sudden surge and recover?Sudden jump up and down10–30 min
    Soak (endurance)Does it leak memory or degrade over time?Moderate load, long hold4–24 h
    ScalabilityDoes adding capacity add throughput?Repeat load at different sizesPer configuration
    ReliabilityDoes it recover from faults?Load + fault injection in non-productionPer scenario
    MetricMeaningNote
    Response time (p50, p90, p95, p99)Time to complete a request, by percentile.Never report only the average; p95 and p99 show the user pain.
    ThroughputRequests (or transactions) per second.Compare with the workload model.
    Error rateFailed requests ÷ total requests.Define “failed” (status ≥ 500, timeout, failed assertion).
    Concurrency (VUs)Simulated simultaneous users.Not the same as registered users.
    SaturationCPU, memory, disk, network, connection pools.Monitor server-side during the test.

    Workload model: worked calculation

    Assumptions agreed with the client and written into the test plan: 10,000 users per day, 20 % of them in the peak hour, each session makes 6 requests, safety factor 2×.

    StepCalculationResult
    Users in peak hour10,000 × 0.202,000 users
    User arrival rate2,000 ÷ 3,600 s0.556 users/s
    Request rate0.556 × 6 requests3.33 requests/s
    Target with safety factor3.33 × 26.67 requests/s
    Concurrent users (Little's law)N = X × R, with X = 0.556 users/s and a 3-minute session (R = 180 s)≈ 100 concurrent sessions
    Controlled conditions are mandatory

    Run performance tests only on an environment the client has authorised in writing, outside business hours or on an isolated environment, with monitoring in place and a named contact who can stop the test. Never load-test production, shared third-party services or systems you do not own. A stress test against an unauthorised system is a denial-of-service attack.

    Example performance script (k6)

    performance/k6-products.js
    // performance/k6-products.js   Run: k6 run performance/k6-products.js
// LOCAL practice API only - never point this at a system you are not authorised to load-test.
import http from 'k6/http';
import { check, sleep } from 'k6';

export const options = {
  stages: [
    { duration: '30s', target: 10 },   // ramp-up
    { duration: '2m',  target: 10 },   // steady state (measure here)
    { duration: '20s', target: 0 },    // ramp-down
  ],
  thresholds: {                         // agreed pass/fail criteria
    http_req_failed:   ['rate<0.01'],   // < 1 % errors
    http_req_duration: ['p(95)<500'],   // 95 % of requests under 500 ms
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.BASE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:8080';

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/products?limit=5`);
  check(res, { 'status is 200': (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);                             // think time
}

    The k6 script was syntax-checked in the build environment but not executed (k6 is not installed there). The equivalent Locust script (performance/locustfile.py) was executed against the local practice API.

    ToolLicenceStrengthsLimitations
    k6 (Grafana)AGPL-3.0 — verify on the official repository and note the copyleft implications before bundling or modifyingScripts in JavaScript, thresholds, CI-friendly, low resource useNo browser rendering by default; protocol-level tests
    Apache JMeterApache-2.0 — verify on the official siteGUI plan builder, many protocols, mature plugins, CLI modeXML plans are hard to review in Git; heavier on resources
    LocustMIT (registry-verified, v2.47.0)Python scripts; web UI; distributedPython GIL limits one process per core
    bash
    # JMeter: build the plan in the GUI, but RUN it headless (non-GUI) for real tests
jmeter -n -t performance/products.jmx -l performance/results.jtl -e -o performance/report/

# Performance report must state: environment, build, data volume, workload model, thresholds,
# results per percentile, errors, server metrics, bottleneck analysis, and limitations.

    Accessibility automation

    automation/ui/test_accessibility.py
    # automation/ui/test_accessibility.py  (axe-core via the Playwright page; axe-core is MPL-2.0, registry-verified)
from pathlib import Path
import json, pytest

AXE = Path("node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js")      # npm i -D axe-core

def test_register_view_has_no_serious_a11y_violations(register_page):
    register_page.open()
    register_page.page.add_script_tag(content=AXE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    result = register_page.page.evaluate("axe.run()")
    serious = [v for v in result["violations"] if v["impact"] in ("serious", "critical")]
    assert not serious, json.dumps([(v["id"], v["help"]) for v in serious], indent=2)

    Lighthouse (Apache-2.0, registry-verified v13.6.0): npx lighthouse http://localhost:8000 --only-categories=accessibility --output=html --output-path=accessibility/lighthouse.html. Treat scores as a screening aid; manual keyboard and screen-reader checks remain mandatory because automated tools detect only part of the possible issues.

    Security test coordination

    StepQA responsibilitySecurity specialist responsibility
    1. ScopeRecord in the test plan which security-relevant behaviours QA will check and which are handed over.Define penetration-test scope, rules of engagement, authorisation.
    2. Safe checks by QAAuthentication required? Role checks? Error messages leak internals? Cookie flags? Password rules? Session timeout?—
    3. EscalateReport suspicion privately to the named security coordinator; do not exploit, do not post in public channels, do not attach real secrets.Triage, reproduce in a safe way, rate (e.g. CVSS), advise fix.
    4. RetestRetest the fix functionally.Verify the vulnerability is closed.
    5. ReportList security observations in the release risk summary.Provide formal assessment report.

    Reference for awareness (not for self-directed attacks): OWASP Top 10 and OWASP ASVS.

    Database validation

    Rules

    Use a test database and a read-only account unless a test case explicitly needs writes. Never connect to production. Never copy production data into test environments without an approved masking process.

    validation.sql
    -- Row-count reconciliation after migration (source vs target)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legacy.customers) AS src, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM app.customers) AS tgt;

-- Orphan check: orders without a customer
SELECT o.id FROM app.orders o LEFT JOIN app.customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;

-- Duplicate check on a business key that must be unique
SELECT email, COUNT(*) FROM app.customers GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

-- Derived value check: order total equals sum of lines (to the paisa)
SELECT o.id FROM app.orders o
JOIN (SELECT order_id, ROUND(SUM(qty * unit_price), 2) AS s FROM app.order_lines GROUP BY order_id) l ON l.order_id = o.id
WHERE ROUND(o.total, 2) <> l.s;

    Each query returns zero rows when the data is correct (except the first, where the two numbers must match). Save the query, the result and the date as evidence.

    Test coverage

    Coverage typeDefinitionCaution
    Requirement coverageRequirements with ≥ 1 executed test ÷ total requirements.Having a test is not the same as having enough tests.
    Risk coverageHigh-risk items tested ÷ high-risk items identified.Needs an agreed risk register.
    Automation coverageAutomated test cases ÷ total test cases (or automated requirement coverage).Say what the denominator is.
    Code coverage (statement/branch)Percentage of code executed by tests (e.g. coverage.py, Apache-2.0; SonarQube shows it).100 % does not prove correctness; do not set it as a vanity target.

    Flaky test management

    A flaky test passes and fails on the same code without changes. Flaky tests destroy trust: people start ignoring red builds.

    Common causeFix
    Fixed sleeps and race conditionsUse auto-waits and web-first assertions.
    Shared or order-dependent dataUnique data per test; independent tests.
    Unstable environment or third-party serviceStub external calls; stabilise the environment; separate contract tests.
    Time, date, locale, randomFreeze time; seed randomness; explicit locale.
    Resource limits in CIRight-size runners; reduce parallelism.
    1. Detect: rerun the failed test 10 times on the same commit; flag as flaky if results differ.
    2. Record in the flaky-test register: ID, first seen, owner, suspected cause, ticket.
    3. Quarantine (tag flaky, run separately, not blocking) for at most 10 working days.
    4. Fix or delete. A quarantined test that is not fixed in time is removed and its coverage gap is listed as risk.
    5. Report the flaky rate every release. Automatic retries are allowed only if every retry is counted and reported.

    Topic packs (ten-part teaching method)

    6.1 Performance testing
    DefinitionMeasuring speed, stability and resource use under defined conditions.
    PurposeSlow or unstable systems lose users and money.
    SetupTest environment, monitoring, k6/JMeter/Locust, written authorisation.
    Procedure1. Agree workload and thresholds. 2. Prepare data. 3. Run baseline. 4. Run measured test. 5. Analyse percentiles and server metrics.
    Expected outputPerformance report with p50/p95/p99, throughput, errors, bottleneck notes.
    VerificationRepeat the run; results within an agreed variance.
    ErrorsTesting a different environment than production-like; average-only reporting.
    ReportingPerformance test report template.
    AssignmentProject 7.
    AssessmentReport review.
    6.2 Load testing
    DefinitionVerifying behaviour at the expected peak load.
    PurposeConfirms launch readiness.
    SetupWorkload model.
    Procedure1. Ramp to peak. 2. Hold steady state. 3. Ramp down. 4. Compare with thresholds.
    Expected outputPass/fail against thresholds.
    VerificationServer metrics show no saturation at peak.
    ErrorsMeasuring during ramp-up.
    ReportingReport.
    AssignmentRun the k6 script on the Practice API.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.3 Stress testing
    DefinitionPushing beyond peak to find the breaking point and failure mode.
    PurposeShows how the system fails and recovers.
    SetupIsolated environment; written approval.
    Procedure1. Increase load stepwise. 2. Note the point errors rise. 3. Reduce load; check recovery.
    Expected outputBreaking-point and recovery description.
    VerificationSystem recovers without manual repair.
    ErrorsRunning on shared/production systems.
    ReportingReport section.
    AssignmentStress the local Practice API; document the limit.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.4 Reliability testing
    DefinitionChecking that the system keeps working or recovers when parts fail.
    PurposeReal systems fail; recovery must be designed and proven.
    SetupNon-production environment; fault-injection plan.
    Procedure1. List failure scenarios (service down, slow dependency, restart). 2. Inject one at a time. 3. Observe behaviour and recovery time.
    Expected outputScenario table with outcomes.
    VerificationNo data loss; user-visible messages are sensible.
    ErrorsInjecting faults without a rollback plan.
    ReportingReliability findings.
    AssignmentStop the API during a UI session; document UI behaviour.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.5 Accessibility testing (advanced)
    DefinitionAutomated and manual audit against WCAG.
    PurposeLegal exposure and inclusive design.
    Setupaxe-core, Lighthouse, screen reader.
    Procedure1. Automate scans for key pages. 2. Add manual checks. 3. Triage by impact and WCAG criterion.
    Expected outputAccessibility report with WCAG mapping.
    VerificationNo unreviewed serious/critical issues.
    ErrorsTreating a Lighthouse score as conformance.
    ReportingReport + defects labelled a11y.
    AssignmentAutomate the scan on three pages.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.6 Security test coordination
    DefinitionOrganising safe security checks with qualified specialists.
    PurposeProtects the client and the company legally.
    SetupScope document; named security coordinator.
    Procedure1. Record scope. 2. Run safe checks. 3. Escalate privately. 4. Retest fixes. 5. Report risk.
    Expected outputSecurity observation log.
    VerificationEscalations acknowledged in writing.
    ErrorsExploiting a finding to “prove it”.
    ReportingPrivate report to coordinator.
    AssignmentComplete the safe-check list for the Practice API.
    AssessmentOral exam on boundaries.
    6.7 Database validation
    DefinitionDirectly verifying data correctness in the database.
    PurposeMany defects are invisible in the UI.
    SetupTest DB, read-only account, SQL client.
    Procedure1. Identify invariants. 2. Write queries returning violations. 3. Run after test and migration steps.
    Expected outputQuery set with zero-row expectations.
    VerificationDeliberately introduce an error in a copy; query must detect it.
    ErrorsTesting against production; writes without approval.
    Reportingevidence/db/.
    AssignmentWrite 8 validation queries for a sample schema.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.8 Test coverage
    DefinitionMeasuring how much of the requirements, risks or code the tests exercise.
    PurposeShows gaps and supports release decisions.
    SetupTraceability matrix; coverage tools.
    Procedure1. Define denominators. 2. Compute. 3. Investigate gaps. 4. Report with context.
    Expected outputCoverage summary.
    VerificationNumbers recomputed by a reviewer match.
    ErrorsChasing a percentage.
    ReportingRelease report.
    AssignmentCompute requirement and automation coverage for A0.
    AssessmentReview.
    6.9 Flaky test management
    DefinitionDetecting, quarantining and fixing nondeterministic tests.
    PurposeProtects the value of automation.
    SetupCI history; flaky register.
    Procedure1. Detect via reruns. 2. Log. 3. Quarantine. 4. Fix or delete. 5. Report rate.
    Expected outputFlaky register and rate trend.
    VerificationRate decreases release over release.
    ErrorsRetrying until green.
    ReportingRegister in docs/.
    AssignmentIntroduce and fix a deliberate race condition.
    AssessmentReview.
    Level 6 exit gate

    Controlled performance report, accessibility automation, database validation set and flaky-test register approved by QA Lead and, for performance, by the Performance Tester role-holder. Sign-off: QA Lead.

    10. Tools We Teach and Use

    Every tool is introduced with installation, licensing, use cases, alternatives and limitations. Licences marked “registry-verified” were read from npm/PyPI metadata on 4 November 2026; all others come from published vendor information that must be re-checked before purchase, bundling or quoting.

    CategoryToolsCost model
    Test managementJira, TestRail or equivalent (Zephyr, Xray, Kiwi TCMS)Commercial / free tiers / open source
    Browser automationPlaywright, SeleniumOpen source (Apache-2.0)
    Web testingBrowser developer toolsFree (built in)
    API testingPostman (+ Newman CLI)Freemium / open-source CLI

    Performancek6, Apache JMeter (+ Locust)Open source (AGPL-3.0 / Apache-2.0 / MIT)

    Tool and licence rules
    • Use only free, permissively licensed or properly purchased software. No cracked or pirated tools — ever.
    • Record every tool, version and licence in the project's THIRD_PARTY.md before first use on a client project.
    • Copyleft licences (GPL, LGPL, AGPL, MPL) are fine for running a tool; ask the QA Lead before bundling, modifying or redistributing one.
    • Before sending client data or builds to a SaaS tool (device cloud, test-management, AI assistants), get the client's written approval and check data residency and retention.
    • Pin versions in lock files; upgrade deliberately and re-run the suite.

    Test management and issue tracking

    Jira (Atlassian)
    CategoryIssue / defect tracking, agile boards
    Use casesDefects, tasks, sprint boards, workflows (the bug lifecycle), dashboards, links to requirements and test runs.
    InstallationCloud service: create a site; no install. Server/Data Center editions are separate products — check Atlassian's current offering.
    Licensing / costProprietary, commercial per-user subscription; a free plan for small teams exists — verify current limits and terms.
    AlternativesGitHub Issues/Projects, YouTrack, Linear, Redmine (open source), Bugzilla (open source).
    LimitationsNeeds admin discipline (fields, workflows); test management needs an add-on; cost grows with users.
    TestRail (or equivalent)
    CategoryTest case management
    Use casesTest cases, suites, runs, results, requirement links, reports. Equivalents: Zephyr, Xray (Jira apps), Qase, Kiwi TCMS.
    InstallationTestRail Cloud (no install) or self-hosted server (vendor instructions). Kiwi TCMS: open-source, run with Docker per its documentation.
    Licensing / costTestRail: proprietary, commercial per-user. Kiwi TCMS: open source (verify licence on its repository). Others vary.
    AlternativesSpreadsheets/CSV in Git (small projects), Xray, Zephyr, Qase, TestLink.
    LimitationsAnother system to maintain; export formats differ; migration between tools is laborious.

    Browser and UI automation

    InstallationChrome DevTools → Lighthouse tab; or npm install -g lighthouse.
    Licensing / costApache-2.0 (registry-verified 2026-11-04: v13.6.0; Lighthouse CI @lhci/cli v0.16.0).
    AlternativesWebPageTest, PageSpeed Insights, axe DevTools.
    LimitationsLab data from one machine; scores vary run to run; accessibility score is not conformance.

    Code quality, version control and CI

    SonarQube
    CategoryStatic code analysis and quality gates
    Use casesFinds bugs, code smells and some vulnerabilities; tracks coverage and duplication; quality gate on pull requests.
    InstallationSelf-host (for example the official Docker image, see SonarSource documentation) and run a scanner (e.g. @sonar/scan) in CI; or use SonarQube Cloud.
    Licensing / costCommunity Build is free and open source (LGPL-3.0 per SonarSource — verify); paid Developer/Enterprise editions add branch/PR analysis and more. Scanner npm package @sonar/scan is LGPL-3.0 (registry-verified 2026-11-04).
    AlternativesSonarQube Cloud, CodeQL, ESLint/Pylint/Ruff, Semgrep.
    LimitationsStatic analysis is not testing; false positives need triage; some features are edition-gated.
    Git and GitHub
    CategoryVersion control and collaboration
    Use casesAll QA assets as code: test cases, scripts, docs, evidence indexes; pull requests; branch protection; issues.
    InstallationInstall Git from git-scm.com (or package manager); create a GitHub account; git config --global user.name / user.email.
    Licensing / costGit: GPL-2.0 (verify). GitHub: SaaS; free and paid plans — verify limits (private repos, Actions minutes, storage).
    AlternativesGitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps.
    LimitationsLarge binary evidence (videos) bloats repos — store in an artefact store and link it.
    GitHub Actions
    CategoryCI/CD automation
    Use casesRun tests on pull request, nightly regression, publish reports, gate merges.
    InstallationAdd YAML files under .github/workflows/ in the repository.
    Licensing / costService with a free allowance that differs for public/private repositories — verify current minutes and limits.
    AlternativesGitLab CI, Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite.
    LimitationsRunner time limits; secrets handling must be disciplined; third-party actions are a supply-chain risk (pin versions).

    Documentation

    Markdown (CommonMark)
    CategoryLightweight documentation format
    Use casesREADMEs, test plans, test cases, reports, defect files — all reviewable in Git.
    InstallationAny text editor; VS Code preview; optional markdownlint for style checks.
    Licensing / costFree. markdownlint-cli is MIT (verify).
    AlternativesAsciiDoc, reStructuredText, Word/Docs (for client-facing formats).
    LimitationsTables are awkward for big matrices (use CSV); no built-in diagrams (use Mermaid or images).

    11. Mandatory Client QA Lifecycle: Stages 01–16

    Every client project follows these 16 stages in order. Each stage lists its objective, responsibilities, inputs, procedure, deliverables, evidence, acceptance criteria and approval gate. A stage is closed only when its gate is signed by the named approver. Stages may overlap in time (for example, automation starts while manual execution continues), but a gate must never be skipped.

    01 Qualification→02 Requirements→03 Strategy→04 Planning→05 Test cases→06 Environment→07 Execution→08 Defects
    09 Automation→10 API / integration→11 Performance→12 Regression→13 UAT→14 Release rec.→15 Prod smoke→16 Maintenance

    Approval gates at a glance

    StageGateApprover
    01 Client QualificationG1 · Proceed / declineTest Manager
    02 Requirement AnalysisG2 · Requirement baselineClient (product owner)
    03 Test StrategyG3 · Strategy approvedTest Manager + client
    04 Test PlanningG4 · Plan approvedTest Manager + client PM
    05 Test Case DevelopmentG5 · Test design approvedQA Lead
    06 Test Environment SetupG6 · Entry gateQA Lead + client tech lead
    07 Manual Test ExecutionG7 · Execution cycle completeQA Lead
    08 Defect ManagementG8 · Defect gate (applies until release)Product owner + QA Lead
    09 Automation DevelopmentG9 · Automation acceptedQA Lead + Automation QA (independent reviewer)
    10 API and Integration TestingG10 · API/integration results acceptedQA Lead
    11 Performance TestingG11a · Pre-run approval / G11b · Report approvalClient (pre-run) · Test Manager (report)
    12 Regression TestingG12 · Regression exitQA Lead
    13 UAT SupportG13 · UAT acceptanceClient business owner
    14 Release RecommendationG14 · Release decisionTest Manager (report) + client release board (decision)
    15 Production Smoke TestingG15 · Post-release confirmationRelease Coordinator + client
    16 MaintenanceG16 · Periodic health reviewQA Lead
    Do not start execution without the entry gate

    Stage 07 must not begin until Gate G6 (environment and entry criteria) is signed. Testing on an unready environment produces false failures, wasted effort and unreliable metrics.

    Role summary across stages (RACI)

    R = responsible, A = accountable, C = consulted, I = informed. “—” means not involved. Each project's test plan may refine this table.

    StageJunior QAManual QAAutomation QAAPI TesterPerf TesterQA LeadTest ManagerRelease Coord.
    01 Qualification—————CA/RI
    02 RequirementsIRCCCAI—
    03 Strategy—CCCCRAI
    04 Planning—CCCCRAC
    05 Test casesRRCC—AI—
    06 EnvironmentIRCCCA/RIC
    07 ExecutionRRII—AII
    08 DefectsRRRRRAII
    09 Automation—CA/RR—AI—
    10 API/integration—CRR—AI—
    11 Performance——CCRCAI
    12 RegressionRRRR—AII
    13 UAT supportIR———A/RIC
    14 Release rec.—CCCCRAC
    15 Production smoke—RC——CIA/R
    16 MaintenanceCRRRCAI—

    Stage 01 — Client Qualification

    ObjectiveDecide whether the engagement is a good fit and understand the product, scope, testing needs and delivery expectations before committing any effort.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Sales / Test Manager
    Accountable: Test Manager
    Consulted: QA Lead
    Informed: Management
    InputsEnquiry, product brief, client contact, any existing documentation.
    Procedure
    1. Hold a discovery call using the qualification questionnaire: product and users, technology stack, release cadence, environments, existing tests, compliance needs, timeline, budget range, decision maker.
    2. Check red flags: “guarantee zero bugs”, “test directly in production”, no test environment, no requirements, nobody owns access, unrealistic deadline.
    3. Assess fit and capacity: skills, tools, devices, availability of the right roles.
    4. Sign a mutual NDA before receiving builds, data or documents.
    5. Record the go / no-go decision and reasons.
    Deliverables and templatesClient Qualification Record; opportunity assessment (fit score, risks); NDA.
    Evidence requiredSigned NDA; call notes; completed questionnaire.
    Acceptance criteriaEvery field is filled or marked “unknown” with an owner and a date.
    Approval gate G1 · Proceed / decline

    Approver: Test Manager. Checks: NDA signed; red flags reviewed; capacity confirmed. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 02 — Requirement Analysis

    ObjectiveUnderstand exactly what the product must do by reviewing specifications, user stories, workflows and acceptance criteria.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead, Manual QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Client product owner
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsSpecifications, user stories, wireframes, workflow diagrams, acceptance criteria, API documentation.
    Procedure
    1. Collect all documents and record their versions.
    2. Walk through the product with the product owner; capture workflows and roles.
    3. Review each requirement with the testability checklist (clear, measurable, complete, consistent, feasible, traceable).
    4. Assign requirement IDs; build the requirement register; classify risk (impact × likelihood).
    5. Log ambiguities, assumptions and questions with an owner and due date.
    6. Agree the requirement baseline (version and date) with the client.
    Deliverables and templatesRequirement register; questions and assumptions log; initial risk register.
    Evidence requiredMeeting notes; list of document versions reviewed; client e-mail confirming the baseline.
    Acceptance criteriaEvery requirement has an ID, a risk rating and a testability verdict; every open question has an owner.
    Approval gate G2 · Requirement baseline

    Approver: Client (product owner). Checks: Baseline confirmed in writing; open questions owned. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 03 — Test Strategy

    ObjectiveChoose the testing types, levels, environments, devices, browsers and tools that address the risks.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead
    Accountable: Test Manager
    Consulted: Client tech lead, Automation QA
    Informed: Delivery team
    InputsRequirement register, risk register, client analytics, budget and timeline.
    Procedure
    1. Map each major risk to a test type and level (unit by developers; API, UI, performance, accessibility by QA).
    2. Define the automation approach: what is automated, when, with which tools.
    3. Define environments and test-data strategy (synthetic data only).
    4. Define the browser/device/OS matrix from the client's analytics.
    5. List tools, licences and costs; check licences against policy.
    6. Define severity and priority scales, defect workflow, metrics and reporting cadence.
    7. State the security-testing boundary and name the client's security coordinator.
    Deliverables and templatesTest Strategy document (template provided).
    Evidence requiredReviewed draft with comments resolved; approval record.
    Acceptance criteriaEach risk has a test response; each in-scope service has a tool and an owner.
    Approval gate G3 · Strategy approved

    Approver: Test Manager + client. Checks: Scope, tools, environments and boundaries agreed. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 04 — Test Planning

    ObjectiveTurn the strategy into an executable plan: scope, schedule, resource allocation, risks, entry and exit criteria.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead
    Accountable: Test Manager
    Consulted: Client project manager
    Informed: Team
    InputsApproved strategy, release schedule, costing sheet.
    Procedure
    1. Write in-scope and out-of-scope lists.
    2. Estimate effort with the costing method (planning, design, execution, automation, retest, reporting, management).
    3. Build the schedule with build dates and milestones; allocate roles.
    4. List risks with mitigations and owners.
    5. Write entry criteria (e.g. build deployed, smoke test passed, data loaded, environment stable) and exit criteria (e.g. all critical cases executed, no open Severity 1/2 without written acceptance).
    6. Define suspension and resumption criteria and the change-control route.
    Deliverables and templatesTest Plan (template provided).
    Evidence requiredPlan version in Git; client acknowledgement.
    Acceptance criteriaEntry and exit criteria are measurable; plan matches the SOW and estimate.
    Approval gate G4 · Plan approved

    Approver: Test Manager + client PM. Checks: Scope, schedule and criteria agreed. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 05 — Test Case Development

    ObjectiveCreate reviewed, traceable test cases linked to requirements.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Manual QA, Junior QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Client (critical cases)
    Informed: Developers
    InputsRequirement register, test strategy, test plan.
    Procedure
    1. Create test scenarios per requirement.
    2. Apply equivalence partitioning, boundary-value analysis, decision tables, state transitions, error guessing.
    3. Write cases with ID, requirement link, preconditions, steps, data, expected result, priority, type tags (smoke, regression, UAT, automation candidate).
    4. Peer-review every case (four-eyes); fix review comments.
    5. Build the requirements traceability matrix (RTM).
    6. Prepare test-data sets with documented purpose.
    Deliverables and templatesTest cases (test-cases/); RTM; test-data specification; automation candidate list.
    Evidence requiredReview log; RTM showing every requirement mapped.
    Acceptance criteria100 % of requirements have at least one case; no case without a requirement; all cases reviewed.
    Approval gate G5 · Test design approved

    Approver: QA Lead. Checks: Coverage and review checks passed. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 06 — Test Environment Setup

    ObjectivePrepare a stable environment with the right build, data, accounts, browsers and devices.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead, client DevOps
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Developers
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsEnvironment requirements, build, access request.
    Procedure
    1. Request or build the environment from the specification; record URL, build number, configuration.
    2. Load synthetic test data; create individual named accounts per role (no shared admin accounts).
    3. Obtain written authorisation for each access granted.
    4. Install and record browser and device versions; verify monitoring and log access.
    5. Agree environment refresh/reset and backup rules.
    6. Run the environment-readiness checklist and a smoke test.
    Deliverables and templatesdocs/test-environment.md; environment-readiness checklist.
    Evidence requiredBuild number screenshot; configuration export; smoke result.
    Acceptance criteriaSmoke test passes; no production data present; access list matches authorisation.
    Approval gate G6 · Entry gate

    Approver: QA Lead + client tech lead. Checks: Environment readiness signed; entry criteria met. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 07 — Manual Test Execution

    ObjectiveExecute the planned test cases and record trustworthy evidence.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Manual QA, Junior QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Developers
    Informed: Client
    InputsApproved cases, ready environment, test data.
    Procedure
    1. Verify entry criteria and the build number; run smoke tests first.
    2. Execute by priority; record Pass / Fail / Blocked / Not run with date, tester, build.
    3. Capture evidence per case (screenshot, video, HAR, log) using the naming convention.
    4. Log defects immediately after reproducing them (Stage 8).
    5. Report daily status: planned, executed, passed, failed, blocked; blockers and risks.
    6. Never edit cases silently — change them through version control with a note.
    Deliverables and templatesExecution log; evidence files; daily status; test execution report.
    Evidence requiredExecution results per case with evidence file names; build identifiers.
    Acceptance criteriaCounts reconcile: passed + failed + blocked + not run = planned.
    Approval gate G7 · Execution cycle complete

    Approver: QA Lead. Checks: Log reviewed for completeness and evidence quality. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 08 — Defect Management

    ObjectiveLog, triage, track and verify defects with reproducible steps, expected and actual results, severity, priority and evidence.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: All testers
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Dev lead, product owner
    Informed: Client
    InputsFailed test results and observations.
    Procedure
    1. Reproduce at least twice; search for duplicates.
    2. Write the defect from the template: title, environment/build, steps, expected, actual, severity, evidence, requirement/test ID.
    3. Propose severity; the product owner sets priority in triage.
    4. Triage on a fixed schedule (daily in execution, otherwise twice weekly).
    5. Retest fixes on the named fixed build, then run related regression; close only after verification.
    6. Escalate stale Severity 1/2 defects; every deferral needs a written decision and appears in the risk summary.
    Deliverables and templatesDefect log; weekly defect summary.
    Evidence requiredDefect history with state changes; retest evidence.
    Acceptance criteriaAll Severity 1/2 defects are fixed and verified, or formally accepted in writing by the product owner.
    Approval gate G8 · Defect gate (applies until release)

    Approver: Product owner + QA Lead. Checks: Open critical defects resolved or waived in writing. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 09 — Automation Development

    ObjectiveAutomate stable, repeatable and valuable test cases.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Automation QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Developers
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsAutomation candidate list, stable build, test data, framework standards.
    Procedure
    1. Select candidates by return on investment and stability.
    2. Set up the framework: Page Object Model, fixtures, configuration through environment variables, reports.
    3. Implement; code-review every pull request.
    4. Run each new test five times locally to expose flakiness.
    5. Integrate with CI; publish JUnit/HTML reports and failure artefacts.
    6. Document how to run the suite; publish the automation coverage report.
    Deliverables and templatesAutomation code in Git; CI workflow; automation coverage report.
    Evidence requiredGreen CI run link; code-review records.
    Acceptance criteriaFlaky rate at or below the agreed target (e.g. 2 %); no secrets in code.
    Approval gate G9 · Automation accepted

    Approver: QA Lead + Automation QA (independent reviewer). Checks: Review passed; CI green; coverage stated honestly. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 10 — API and Integration Testing

    ObjectiveValidate data exchange, authentication, error handling and dependencies between components and systems.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: API Tester
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Developers, client integrators
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsAPI specification (OpenAPI or document), credentials for test environment, integration diagrams.
    Procedure
    1. Build the API collection: positive, negative, authentication, boundary, schema checks.
    2. Design integration scenarios: sequence, data mapping, retry, timeout, idempotency, failure of a dependency.
    3. Stub or virtualise unavailable dependencies.
    4. Verify data consistency in the test database with read-only queries.
    5. Check error bodies and logs for sensitive-data leakage.
    6. Hand security-relevant observations to the security coordinator.
    Deliverables and templatesAPI test collection and automation; integration test report; schema files.
    Evidence requiredRequest/response captures with tokens removed; Newman/pytest report.
    Acceptance criteriaAll specified status codes provoked; schema validation passes or defects raised.
    Approval gate G10 · API/integration results accepted

    Approver: QA Lead. Checks: Critical defects resolved or waived; security observations handed over. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 11 — Performance Testing

    ObjectiveEstablish workload assumptions, baselines and thresholds, then test under controlled conditions.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Performance Tester
    Accountable: Test Manager
    Consulted: Client DevOps, developers
    Informed: Client
    InputsNon-functional requirements, analytics, environment sizing, authorisation.
    Procedure
    1. Agree non-functional targets and the workload model in writing (see worked calculation).
    2. Confirm the environment, data volume, monitoring and a named person who can stop the test.
    3. Script and validate with one user; record the baseline.
    4. Run load (and stress/soak/spike if in scope) with ramp-up, steady state and ramp-down.
    5. Collect client-side and server-side metrics; analyse percentiles, errors, saturation.
    6. Report results, bottlenecks and limitations; never extrapolate beyond what was measured.
    Deliverables and templatesPerformance test plan, scripts, raw results, performance test report.
    Evidence requiredResult files; monitoring screenshots; environment description.
    Acceptance criteriaThresholds met, or gaps documented with recommendations.
    Approval gate G11a · Pre-run approval / G11b · Report approval

    Approver: Client (pre-run) · Test Manager (report). Checks: Authorisation and workload model signed before running. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 12 — Regression Testing

    ObjectiveVerify that changes have not broken existing functionality.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Manual QA, Automation QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Developers
    Informed: Client
    InputsChange list, regression suite, fixed build.
    Procedure
    1. Perform change-impact analysis; map changes to requirements and cases.
    2. Select the suite: changed areas, integrating areas, critical paths, rotating sample.
    3. Run automated and manual regression on the release candidate.
    4. Classify each failure: product defect, test defect, flaky test, environment issue.
    5. Retest fixes; update the RTM; record skipped tests with reasons.
    Deliverables and templatesRegression execution report.
    Evidence requiredRun IDs; reports; defect links.
    Acceptance criteriaAll critical-path tests pass; every failure is explained.
    Approval gate G12 · Regression exit

    Approver: QA Lead. Checks: Regression exit criteria from the plan are met. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 13 — UAT Support

    ObjectiveAssist the client's business users to perform acceptance testing.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead, Manual QA
    Accountable: Client product owner
    Consulted: Developers
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsQA exit report, UAT scope, business users and schedule.
    Procedure
    1. Agree UAT scope and entry criteria (QA exit met).
    2. Write UAT scripts in business language; prepare accounts, data and the environment.
    3. Brief users; provide a support channel during UAT.
    4. Log UAT issues in the same tracker with a UAT label; triage with the client daily.
    5. Retest fixes; report UAT status; obtain the signed UAT acceptance.
    Deliverables and templatesUAT plan; UAT scripts; UAT report.
    Evidence requiredCompleted UAT scripts; issue list; signed acceptance.
    Acceptance criteriaClient business owner signs UAT acceptance or lists conditions.
    Approval gate G13 · UAT acceptance

    Approver: Client business owner. Checks: Signed UAT report. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 14 — Release Recommendation

    ObjectiveProvide an evidence-based QA status and an honest unresolved-risk summary to support the release decision.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: QA Lead
    Accountable: Test Manager
    Consulted: Release Coordinator, client release board
    Informed: Management
    InputsAll test results, defect log, metrics, UAT report, waiver records.
    Procedure
    1. Compile metrics: execution %, pass rate, open defects by severity, requirement coverage, automation results, performance and accessibility findings.
    2. List unresolved risks and waivers with owners.
    3. Compare results with the exit criteria in the plan.
    4. Draft the recommendation: Go, Conditional Go (with conditions) or No-Go. The decision belongs to the client's release board; QA recommends.
    5. Second-person review by the Test Manager; present and record the decision.
    Deliverables and templatesRelease QA report; QA sign-off checklist.
    Evidence requiredMetrics source data; signed checklist.
    Acceptance criteriaNumbers reconcile with source data; no metric is selectively omitted.
    Approval gate G14 · Release decision

    Approver: Test Manager (report) + client release board (decision). Checks: Independent review done; decision recorded. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 15 — Production Smoke Testing

    ObjectiveAfter deployment, verify the agreed critical functions with minimal, safe actions.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Release Coordinator, Manual QA
    Accountable: Release Coordinator
    Consulted: Client DevOps
    Informed: Client
    InputsAgreed production smoke list, test accounts, deployment window, rollback criteria.
    Procedure
    1. Agree before the release: the smoke list, accounts, window, who may decide a rollback.
    2. Use dedicated test accounts and read-only or reversible actions only; no load; no data clean-up in production without approval.
    3. Execute immediately after deployment; capture evidence.
    4. Report within 30 minutes: pass, or fail with evidence and impact.
    5. If rollback criteria are met, the client's authorised person decides; QA provides facts.
    Deliverables and templatesProduction smoke report.
    Evidence requiredTimestamped screenshots; build/version page.
    Acceptance criteriaAll listed functions pass or a documented rollback/hot-fix decision exists.
    Approval gate G15 · Post-release confirmation

    Approver: Release Coordinator + client. Checks: Smoke pass confirmed or rollback decided. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Stage 16 — Maintenance

    ObjectiveKeep the test suites accurate, fast and trustworthy: update tests, remove obsolete ones and monitor flaky automation.
    ResponsibilitiesResponsible: Automation QA, Manual QA
    Accountable: QA Lead
    Consulted: Client
    Informed: Test Manager
    InputsRelease notes, new requirements, CI history, flaky register.
    Procedure
    1. After each release update cases, RTM and automation for changed behaviour.
    2. Retire obsolete tests (record the reason).
    3. Review the flaky register; fix or delete within the policy time.
    4. Hold a quarterly suite-health review: runtime, flaky rate, coverage, maintenance cost.
    5. Upgrade tool and dependency versions deliberately; re-run the suite.
    6. Send the monthly retainer report and hold a lessons-learned review.
    Deliverables and templatesUpdated suites; monthly maintenance report; suite-health review.
    Evidence requiredCommit history; CI trend; flaky register.
    Acceptance criteriaSuite remains green on the main branch; flaky rate within target.
    Approval gate G16 · Periodic health review

    Approver: QA Lead. Checks: Review minutes filed; client acknowledges the report. Record the decision (approved / approved with conditions / rejected), date and approver name in docs/qa-signoff.md.

    Change control during a project

    1. Any change to scope, schedule, environments or exit criteria is raised in writing.
    2. The QA Lead assesses impact on effort, risk and dates using the costing method.
    3. The client approves the revised plan/quote.
    4. The Test Plan version is incremented and filed before work on the change starts.

    12. Professional QA Repository Structure

    Every client project has one repository (or one folder in the client's repository) with this structure. A ready-made skeleton is supplied in qa-project-template/.

    qa-project/
    qa-project/
├── README.md                     # purpose, how to run, owners, links
├── THIRD_PARTY.md                # every tool + version + licence
├── docs/
│   ├── test-strategy.md
│   ├── test-plan.md
│   ├── requirements-traceability.md
│   ├── test-environment.md
│   ├── release-report.md
│   └── qa-signoff.md
├── test-cases/
│   ├── functional/
│   ├── regression/
│   ├── integration/
│   └── acceptance/
├── automation/
│   ├── ui/                       # Playwright / Selenium / Cypress tests
│   ├── api/                      # pytest + requests, Postman/Newman
│   ├── fixtures/
│   ├── page-objects/
│   └── reports/                  # generated; git-ignored
├── performance/                  # k6 / JMeter scripts, results summaries
├── accessibility/                # axe / Lighthouse configs and findings
├── test-data/                    # synthetic data only
├── evidence/                     # screenshots, logs (index in Git, bulk in artefact store)
├── defects/                      # defect reports (if not in a tracker)
└── .github/
    └── workflows/                # CI pipelines
    FolderContentsRules
    docs/Strategy, plan, traceability matrix, environment description, release report, QA sign-off.Markdown, one file per document, version in the header, changes through pull requests.
    test-cases/Cases grouped by type: functional, regression, integration, acceptance.One CSV or Markdown file per feature; ID pattern TC-<area>-<nnn>; each case links a REQ- ID.
    automation/ui, apiExecutable tests.Independent tests; no secrets; code review before merge.
    automation/page-objects, fixturesReusable page classes and fixtures.Locators and actions only; fixtures documented.
    automation/reports/JUnit XML, HTML, traces.Generated; listed in .gitignore; published as CI artefacts.
    performance/Scripts, workload model, result summaries.Raw result files > 5 MB go to the artefact store.
    accessibility/Scan configuration, WCAG findings, manual-check records.Findings reference WCAG success criteria.
    test-data/Synthetic data files and a README.Never real personal data or production extracts.
    evidence/Index of evidence and small files.Name pattern <date>_<TC-id>_<result>_<n>.<ext>; large videos live in the artefact store, linked from the index.
    defects/Defect write-ups when no tracker is available.One file per defect: DEF-nnn.md.
    .github/workflows/CI pipelines.Secrets only via CI secret store.
    Never commit these
    • Passwords, API keys, access tokens, private keys, certificates, .env files with real values.
    • Sensitive customer data or personal data of any real person.
    • Production database extracts or dumps, even “just a small sample”.
    • Unsanitised HAR files, screenshots showing tokens, e-mails or personal data.
    • Client confidential documents in public repositories.

    If a secret is committed by accident

    1. Stop and tell the QA Lead immediately; do not try to hide it.
    2. Revoke or rotate the secret at its source first (the commit history cannot be trusted to be private).
    3. Remove it from the repository history using the approved procedure from the QA Lead (rewriting history is a controlled operation).
    4. Record an incident note: what, when, who was told, what was rotated.
    5. Add a prevention step (pre-commit secret scan, push protection, .gitignore rule).

    Starter .gitignore for QA repositories

    .gitignore
    # secrets and local config
.env
*.pem
*.key
secrets/
# generated output
automation/reports/
playwright-report/

    Writing standards

    • Every document starts with a header block: ID, title, version, status (draft / in review / approved), author, reviewer, date.
    • Use plain, unambiguous language. Avoid “works correctly”, “should be fine”, “etc.”, “as expected”.
    • State numbers with units and the date/build they refer to.
    • Cite evidence by file name or link; do not paste unreferenced claims.
    • Separate facts (observed), interpretation (what it means) and recommendation (what we suggest).
    • Version every change; approved documents change only through a new version with a change note.
    • Mark client-confidential documents and store them only in approved locations.

    Status and approval vocabulary

    StatusMeaning
    DraftAuthor is still writing; not for client use.
    In reviewInternal or client review in progress; comments tracked.
    ApprovedSigned by the named approver; baseline for further work.
    SupersededReplaced by a newer approved version; retained for history.

    14. QA Metrics

    Metrics support decisions; they are not a scorecard for people. Every metric has a written formula, a data source and an owner before the project starts.

    MetricFormulaWorked exampleReading it correctly
    Test execution %executed ÷ planned × 100, where executed = passed + failed(342+30) ÷ 400 = 93.0 %Progress. Blocked and not-run cases are listed separately.
    Pass ratepassed ÷ executed × 100342 ÷ 372 = 91.9 %Quality signal for the executed scope only.
    Fail ratefailed ÷ executed × 10030 ÷ 372 = 8.1 %Pass rate + fail rate = 100 %.
    Defect densityvalid defects ÷ size (KLOC, function points or requirements)46 ÷ 23 KLOC = 2.0 per KLOCCompare like with like (same size unit, same period).
    Defect leakagedefects found after release ÷ (found in QA + found after release) × 1004 ÷ (46+4) = 8.0 %Defect-removal efficiency = 100 − leakage = 92.0 %.
    Defect reopening ratereopened ÷ fixed × 1006 ÷ 40 = 15.0 %High values point at fix quality or poor retest steps.
    Requirement coveragerequirements with ≥ 1 executed test ÷ total requirements × 100114 ÷ 120 = 95.0 %List the uncovered requirements by name.
    Automation coverageautomated cases ÷ total cases × 100 (state the denominator)160 ÷ 400 = 40.0 %Also report automation pass rate and runtime.
    Flaky test ratetests with inconsistent results ÷ automated tests × 1008 ÷ 160 = 5.0 %Target example: ≤ 2 %; trend matters.
    Mean time to detect (MTTD)average of (detection time − time the defect was introduced / build delivered)(1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 4.5) ÷ 5 = 2.5 daysShorter means earlier testing.
    Mean time to resolve (MTTR)average of (closure time − report time)(2 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 7.5) ÷ 5 = 4.5 daysReport by severity; do not mix S1 with S4.

    Example data used above: 400 planned cases = 342 passed + 30 failed + 8 blocked + 20 not run; 46 valid defects found in QA and 4 in production; 40 defects fixed, 6 reopened.

    Why metrics must never be manipulated

    A metric that is gamed stops measuring quality and starts hiding risk. The cost surfaces later: a release goes live with unknown defects, the client loses trust, and the company's evidence becomes worthless in a dispute. We report the truth, including bad news, as early as possible.

    Common manipulations and the controls that prevent them

    ManipulationWhy it is wrongControl
    Counting “not run” or blocked cases as passedInflates pass rate and execution %.Formula fixed in advance; counts must reconcile to the planned total.
    Splitting one test into many (or merging many) to change countsCase counts become meaningless.Test-case design standard; review for atomicity; report requirement coverage next to case counts.
    Lowering severity or relabelling defects as “enhancements”Makes the open-defect picture look better.Severity defined by the table, challenged in triage; changes need a recorded reason.
    Closing defects without verified retestDefect counts fall while risk remains.Only the tester closes; closure needs build number and evidence.
    Excluding failed or flaky tests from the denominatorPass rate appears higher.Report flaky tests separately and keep them in the totals.
    Reporting average response time onlyHides the slow tail users experience.Always give p90, p95, p99 and error rate.
    Rewarding people for defect counts or pass percentagesEncourages gaming and conflict with developers.Appraise report quality, reproducibility, coverage and teamwork instead.
    Selecting the “good” builds or runsCherry-picking.Publish all runs of the cycle; keep raw data in the repository.
    Rules for honest reporting
    • Publish the formula, the date, the build and the data source next to every number.
    • A second person reconciles the report to raw data before it leaves the company.
    • Show trends, not only snapshots; explain context (for example, test scope changed).
    • If a target is missed, say so, explain why, and state the risk and the recommended action.
    • Never present a metric as proof that the product is “safe” or “bug-free”.

    15. Costing and Pricing

    How to cost a QA engagement from first principles, convert cost into a selling price, and check profitability. All rupee figures here are illustrative assumptions that show the method; replace them with the company's real salaries, utilisation, vendor quotes and tax rules before quoting any client.

    Cost components

    ComponentHow to calculate
    Test planning hoursStrategy + plan + estimate + risk register effort (QA Lead and Manual QA).
    Manual testing hoursRequirement analysis + test design + environment support + execution cycles + defect handling.
    Automation developmentCandidates × average build time per test + framework set-up + CI + review + stabilisation.
    Test environment costsCloud environment (instances, storage, data transfer) for the period, or client-provided (then 0, with an assumption).
    Device and browser costsDevice-cloud plan, purchased devices (depreciation over use period), OS licences.
    Tool licencesSeats × price × months for commercial tools; open-source tools cost 0 licence but still cost set-up time.
    Performance infrastructureLoad-generator machines, monitoring, data volume, test-run hours.
    ReportingReport preparation, review, client presentations.
    RetestingDefect retests and regression after fixes (typically 15–25 % of execution effort).
    MaintenanceSuite updates after releases; flaky test fixes; tool upgrades (charged as retainer or per release).
    Project managementPlanning, status reporting, meetings, client communication (5–15 % of delivery hours).
    ContingencyAllowance for uncertainty; 10–20 % depending on requirement stability and access risk.

    Step 1 — Hourly cost rate per role

    formula
    cost per productive hour = monthly cost-to-company (CTC) ÷ productive hours per month
productive hours             = 160 working hours × 80 % utilisation = 128
Example (Manual QA):  ₹45,000 ÷ 128 = ₹351.56  →  rounded ₹352 per hour
