    Step 3 — Cost, price, margins

    LineCalculationAmount
    Labour570 h at an average ₹474/h₹2,70,456
    Non-labour direct costsTable above₹31,000
    Contingency10 % × (₹2,70,456 + ₹31,000)₹30,146
    Total delivery cost (COGS)Labour + non-labour + contingency₹3,31,602
    Selling price (ex-tax)COGS ÷ (1 − 0.40), rounded to ₹1,000₹5,53,000
    Gross profitPrice − COGS₹2,21,398
    Gross marginGross profit ÷ Price40.0 %
    Variable costsNon-labour direct costs (salaried labour is fixed in the short term)₹31,000
    ContributionPrice − variable costs₹5,22,000
    Contribution marginContribution ÷ Price94.4 %
    Gross margin versus contribution margin

    Gross margin shows profitability after all direct costs including salaried labour. Contribution margin shows what the project adds towards fixed costs after only the costs that vary with taking the project (environments, licences, infrastructure, subcontractors). A project can have a modest gross margin yet a high contribution margin; use both.

    Step 4 — Break-even

    formula
    Break-even (projects/month) = monthly fixed costs ÷ contribution per project
Fixed costs (illustrative) = team CTC ₹5,10,000 + overheads ₹1,50,000 = ₹6,60,000 per month
Contribution per project   = ₹5,22,000
Break-even                 = ₹6,60,000 ÷ ₹5,22,000 = 1.26 projects of this size per month

Break-even in billable hours = 1.26 × 570 h = 721 hours per month
Team capacity                = 7 people × 128 productive hours = 896 hours = 1.57 projects
Break-even uses 80 % of capacity  →  margin of safety = 20 %

    Interpretation: below the break-even volume the department makes a loss however good each project's gross margin looks. Here break-even already needs about four-fifths of the team's capacity, which leaves little room for bench time, sickness, training or a delayed client. Track break-even and utilisation every month; they set the pipeline target.

    Sensitivity of price to target margin

    Target gross marginPrice = COGS ÷ (1 − margin)Price vs 40 % case
    30 %₹4,74,000-14.3 %
    35 %₹5,10,000-7.8 %
    40 %₹5,53,000+0.0 %
    50 %₹6,63,000+19.9 %

    Four pricing models

    ModelHow the price is setBest forMain risk and control
    Project-basedEstimate by activity (above) → price with milestones (e.g. 30 % at plan approval, 40 % at execution complete, 30 % at sign-off).Defined releases with clear scopeScope creep → change-request procedure; milestones tied to approval gates.
    Fixed-scopeFixed price for an explicit scope list (features, platforms, cycles). Includes contingency and a risk premium. Extra cycles or scope are priced at the rate card.Clients who need budget certainty and have stable requirementsUnder-estimation → strict assumptions, exclusions, maximum cycles (e.g. 2 execution + 1 retest cycle).
    Time-based (T&M)Role day/hour rates × actual timesheets, with an optional cap. Rates from the table above.Uncertain scope, discovery work, staff augmentationClient budget anxiety → weekly timesheets, burn-down report, agreed cap and approval above cap.
    Monthly QA retainerCommitted hours per month at a blended rate + tool pass-through; unused hours expire (or roll over by agreement); overage at an agreed rate.Continuous releases, maintenance, regression upkeepUnder-use or over-use → monthly utilisation report; quarterly re-sizing.

    Retainer worked example

    RoleHours/monthCost/hourCost
    QA Lead8₹781₹6,248
    Manual QA Engineer40₹352₹14,080
    Automation QA Engineer24₹547₹13,128
    API Tester8₹469₹3,752
    Tools and reporting pass-through——₹5,000
    Total cost to deliver80₹42,208
    formula
    Retainer price (35 % target margin, steady work) = ₹42,208 ÷ (1 − 0.35) = ₹64,935  →  quote ₹65,000 per month for 80 committed hours
Margin check = (₹65,000 − ₹42,208) ÷ ₹65,000 = 35.1 %
Overage rate (blended cost per hour ₹465 ÷ (1 − 0.40)) ≈ ₹800 per extra hour
    Quoting rules
    • Quote only from a written estimate; list assumptions and exclusions in the proposal.
    • Verify every tool licence and cloud cost on the vendor's current price page on the day of quoting.
    • Add taxes (e.g. GST) as separate lines according to current rules; never bury them.
    • Never promise outcomes (“zero defects”, “100 % automation”); sell evidence, coverage and risk reduction.
    • A second person (Test Manager) reviews every quote before it is sent.

    16. Employee Roles

    Eight roles define who does what. A person may hold more than one role on a small project, but the reviewer of any work product must never be its author.

    Junior QA Tester→Manual QA Engineer→Automation QA / API Tester / Performance Tester→QA Lead→Test Manager
    RoleOne-line purposePrimary level gate
    Junior QA TesterExecute and report under supervision.Levels 1–2
    Manual QA EngineerDesign and run risk-based manual tests.Levels 1–3
    Automation QA EngineerBuild maintainable automation and CI.Levels 1–5
    API TesterValidate interfaces and integrations.Levels 1–4
    Performance TesterRun controlled performance campaigns.Levels 1–6
    QA LeadOwn quality approach and technical sign-off.All levels + leadership assessment
    Test ManagerOwn governance, budget and client trust.Management assessment
    Release CoordinatorCoordinate release readiness and sign-off.Levels 1–2 + release process assessment
    Separation of duties

    Author ≠ reviewer. The tester who ran a test does not approve its sign-off; the QA Lead who wrote the recommendation does not approve it alone; the person who prepared a quote does not approve it. This is the department's main protection against errors and against pressure to “make the numbers look good”.

    Role cards

    Junior QA Tester
    PurposeExecute test cases, record evidence and report defects accurately under supervision.
    Core responsibilities
    • Execute assigned test cases and exploratory sessions; record Pass / Fail / Blocked with evidence.
    • Log defects with reproducible steps; retest fixes.
    • Prepare and maintain synthetic test data; update traceability rows.
    • Write the daily learning journal; follow the 90-day plan.
    Skills requiredLevel 1–2 knowledge; careful, honest, observant; reads requirements; basic Git; clear written English.
    Typical deliverablesExecuted cases with evidence; defect reports; daily status line.
    Next step in careerManual QA Engineer after Levels 1–3 + two supervised projects.
    Manual QA Engineer
    PurposeDesign and execute risk-based manual tests independently across web, mobile and desktop.
    Core responsibilities
    • Analyse requirements; raise questions; design cases with EP, BVA, decision tables, state transitions.
    • Run smoke, regression, exploratory and UAT-support sessions.
    • Review juniors' cases and defects; maintain the RTM.
    • Run cross-browser, responsive and first-line accessibility checks.
    Skills requiredLevels 1–3; strong technique knowledge; developer tools; SQL basics; coaching skills.
    Typical deliverablesTest cases, RTM, execution reports, exploratory notes.
    Next step in careerAutomation QA Engineer, API Tester or QA Lead.
    Automation QA Engineer
    PurposeBuild and maintain reliable UI and API automation integrated with CI.
    Core responsibilities
    • Select automation candidates by ROI; build frameworks (POM, fixtures, data factories).
    • Write and review Playwright/Selenium/Cypress and pytest code; keep flaky rate low.
    • Maintain CI pipelines and reports; publish automation coverage.
    • Mentor testers in automation practices.
    Skills requiredLevel 5; one programming language well; Git, CI/CD; debugging; clean-code habits.
    Typical deliverablesAutomation code, CI workflows, automation coverage report, flaky register.
    Next step in careerQA Lead or Test Architect.
    API Tester
    PurposeValidate service interfaces, integrations, data exchange, authentication and errors.
    Core responsibilities
    • Build Postman/pytest suites with schema validation and negative testing.
    • Verify integration scenarios, retries, timeouts, idempotency.
    • Validate data in the test database with read-only queries.
    • Hand security-relevant observations to the security coordinator.
    Skills requiredLevel 4; HTTP, JSON, OAuth/JWT basics; SQL; scripting.
    Typical deliverablesAPI collections/tests, integration report, schemas.
    Next step in careerAutomation QA Engineer or Performance Tester.
    Performance Tester
    PurposePlan and run controlled performance, load and stress tests and analyse bottlenecks.
    Core responsibilities
    • Agree workload models and thresholds in writing.
    • Script and execute k6/JMeter/Locust tests in authorised environments.
    • Collect client and server metrics; analyse percentiles, errors and saturation.
    • Write the performance test report with limitations.
    Skills requiredLevel 6; statistics basics; Linux and monitoring; networking; scripting.
    Typical deliverablesWorkload model, scripts, performance report.
    Next step in careerQA Lead or Performance Architect.
    QA Lead
    PurposeOwn the quality approach and delivery of QA on projects; coach the team; sign recommendations.
    Core responsibilities
    • Write strategy and plan; estimate effort; assign work.
    • Review test design, automation and reports; run triage.
    • Sign the QA release recommendation (second reviewer: Test Manager).
    • Coach and assess trainees at level gates; keep the team honest on metrics.
    Skills requiredAll levels; technical depth plus communication, estimation, risk thinking and leadership.
    Typical deliverablesStrategy, plan, reports, approvals, coaching notes.
    Next step in careerTest Manager.
    Test Manager
    PurposeOwn QA commercial and delivery governance across projects: scope, budget, staffing, quality of reporting.
    Core responsibilities
    • Qualify clients and approve proposals, quotes and change requests.
    • Allocate people and budget; manage margin, utilisation and break-even.
    • Approve strategies/plans; act as independent reviewer of release recommendations.
    • Handle escalations; own client relationships and department improvement.
    Skills requiredManagement and commercial skills; strong QA background; contracts and risk.
    Typical deliverablesQuotes, portfolio dashboard, approvals, improvement plan.
    Next step in careerHead of Delivery / Quality.
    Release Coordinator
    PurposeCoordinate release readiness, sign-off paperwork and production smoke testing with the client.
    Core responsibilities
    • Maintain the release calendar and checklists; chase approvals.
    • Organise production smoke tests and rollback decision points with the client.
    • Collect evidence and file the QA sign-off package.
    • Communicate status to all stakeholders clearly and on time.
    Skills requiredProcess discipline; communication; basic testing knowledge; configuration/release management concepts.
    Typical deliverablesRelease checklist, sign-off package, production smoke report.
    Next step in careerTest Manager or Delivery Manager.

    17. Practical Employee Projects

    Eight projects take the trainee from manual testing to a complete client QA report. Each project is marked on the same rubric and must be reviewed by a person other than its author. Targets are the local practice systems or an explicitly authorised site.

    #ProjectLevelTimePrimary deliverable
    1Test a business website manuallyLevel 35 daysdocs/test-plan.md (lite)
    2Prepare a complete test case suiteLevel 25 daystest-cases/functional/shop.csv
    3Test a REST APILevel 45 daysautomation/api/postman/collection.json
    4Automate browser tests with PlaywrightLevel 55 daysautomation/ui/
    5Automate API testsLevel 54 daysautomation/api/
    6Create a regression suiteLevel 2 + 53 daystest-cases/regression/
    7Perform a controlled performance testLevel 64 daysperformance/ scripts
    8Prepare a complete client QA reportAll levels5 daysComplete qa-project/ repository
    Authorisation first

    Only test the Practice Shop and Practice API (running on your own machine) or a site whose owner has authorised testing in writing. Never run automation, load or scanning tools against public websites, third-party APIs or shared systems without that authorisation.

    Project 1 — Test a business website manually

    Level / time-boxLevel 3 · 5 days
    Target systemThe company's own website, or a client site with written authorisation, or a public practice site. No authorisation, no testing.
    Tasks
    1. Write a one-page scope and test approach (what is in/out, browsers, devices, data).
    2. Build a sitemap; list user journeys and risks.
    3. Design and execute at least 40 test cases: navigation, links, forms, content, responsive layout (360/768/1280 px), cross-browser (two browsers), first-line accessibility.
    4. Log every defect with evidence; rate severity and priority.
    5. Write the test execution report with an honest risk statement.
    Deliverables (repository paths)docs/test-plan.md (lite), test-cases/functional/website.csv, evidence/, defects/, docs/test-execution-report.md.
    Acceptance criteriaEvery case executed with evidence; ≥ 5 reproducible defects or documented zero-defect reasoning; counts reconcile; report states what was not tested.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 2 — Prepare a complete test case suite

    Level / time-boxLevel 2 · 5 days
    Target systemVEL Practice Shop, shop/cart/session/logout modules (REQ-010 to REQ-014) plus registration regression.
    Tasks
    1. Create the requirements traceability matrix.
    2. Apply EP, BVA, decision table, state transition and error guessing; name the technique on each case.
    3. Write at least 60 test cases across functional, negative, boundary, session and accessibility types, each linked to a requirement.
    4. Tag cases: smoke, regression, UAT, automation candidate.
    5. Arrange a four-eyes review with a colleague; record and resolve every comment.
    Deliverables (repository paths)test-cases/functional/shop.csv, docs/requirements-traceability.md, review log.
    Acceptance criteria100 % requirement coverage; no duplicate cases; ≥ 25 % of cases are negative or boundary; review comments closed.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 3 — Test a REST API

    Level / time-boxLevel 4 · 5 days
    Target systemVEL Practice API (qa-project-template/practice-api) running locally.
    Tasks
    1. Read the contract and build a Postman collection with ≥ 40 requests.
    2. Cover positive, negative, authentication, boundary, schema and method tests for every endpoint.
    3. Add assertions on status, headers, body, schema and response time.
    4. Raise a defect for each deviation, with request/response evidence (tokens removed).
    5. Hand over any access-control observation as a security escalation note, not a public defect.
    Deliverables (repository paths)automation/api/postman/collection.json, defects, docs/api-test-report.md.
    Acceptance criteria≥ 8 correct defects; no false defects against a documented behaviour; all endpoints covered; escalation note present.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 4 — Automate browser tests with Playwright

    Level / time-boxLevel 5 · 5 days
    Target systemVEL Practice Shop UI.
    Tasks
    1. Set up Playwright with pytest; configure base URL through an environment variable.
    2. Create page objects for Register, Login and Shop.
    3. Automate ≥ 15 tests including parametrised boundary tests; mark known defects xfail(strict=True) with the defect ID.
    4. Run on Chromium and Firefox; enable trace on first retry/failure.
    5. Run each test 5 times; fix or remove any flaky test; document how to run.
    Deliverables (repository paths)automation/ui/, automation/page-objects/, automation/fixtures/, HTML/JUnit report.
    Acceptance criteriaSuite green on 5 consecutive runs; no sleeps; no secrets; code review passed.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 5 — Automate API tests

    Level / time-boxLevel 5 · 4 days
    Target systemVEL Practice API.
    Tasks
    1. Create session fixtures for base URL and token (credentials from environment variables).
    2. Write ≥ 15 pytest tests, including JSON-schema validation of products.
    3. Mark seeded defects as strict xfail with defect IDs.
    4. Generate JUnit XML; run in CI.
    5. Report automation coverage against the Level-4 manual cases.
    Deliverables (repository paths)automation/api/, automation/api/schemas/, CI run link, coverage note.
    Acceptance criteriaIndependent tests; zero shared state; schema checks present; CI green.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 6 — Create a regression suite

    Level / time-boxLevel 2 + 5 · 3 days
    Target systemPractice Shop build 1.0 vs build 1.1 (?build=1.1).
    Tasks
    1. Classify tests into tiers: smoke (≤ 15 min), regression (nightly), full (weekly).
    2. Write selection rules and a change-impact table.
    3. Run the suite on build 1.0 (baseline) and build 1.1.
    4. Compare results; identify fixed defects, new regressions, and obsolete tests.
    5. Report with a go/no-go style recommendation for build 1.1.
    Deliverables (repository paths)test-cases/regression/, docs/regression-report.md, updated RTM.
    Acceptance criteriaAt least one regression found and explained; every skipped test justified; recommendation supported by evidence.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 7 — Perform a controlled performance test

    Level / time-boxLevel 6 · 4 days
    Target systemVEL Practice API on localhost only (never a shared or third-party system).
    Tasks
    1. Write a one-page performance test plan: objectives, workload model (use the worked formula), thresholds (e.g. p95 < 500 ms, errors < 1 %), environment, data, stop conditions.
    2. Script GET /api/products and GET /api/slow?delay=200 in k6, JMeter or Locust; validate with one user.
    3. Run baseline (1 VU), then load at 10, 25 and 50 VUs with ramp-up, steady state and ramp-down.
    4. Record client metrics and the server's CPU/memory (e.g. top).
    5. Report p50/p95/p99, throughput, errors, bottleneck notes and limitations (local machine, synthetic data).
    Deliverables (repository paths)performance/ scripts, results summary, docs/performance-report.md.
    Acceptance criteriaPlan approved before running; steady-state only is measured; limitations stated; no claim beyond measured data.
    Marking (100 points)Planning and approach 15 · Technical quality 30 · Evidence and traceability 20 · Reporting honesty 20 · Professional conduct and timeliness 15. Pass: 70.

    Project 8 — Prepare a complete client QA report

    Level / time-boxAll levels · 5 days

    18. 90-Day Employee Training Plan

    Thirteen weeks (65 working days, about 90 calendar days) take a beginner from zero to a supervised, productive QA professional. Each week has daily focus areas, a required deliverable and a review gate. Use it with the Practical Workbook.

    If the trainee falls behind

    1. Identify the gap with the buddy within two working days; check understanding, not just output.
    2. Add a focused coaching block (maximum 5 working days) with a specific exercise and a re-test.
    3. If the gap remains after the re-test, the QA Lead and Test Manager agree a revised plan in writing.
    4. Never lower an assessment pass mark to keep a schedule.

    Final evidence checklist (Day 90)

    • Learning repository with 90 daily journal entries.
    • All level-gate records signed.
    • Projects 1–8 with scores ≥ 70 and reviewer names.
    • Capstone repository complete and reproducible.
    • Final assessment papers and practical marksheets filed.
    • Management decision and development plan recorded.

    19. Assessment and Competency Framework

    How the department decides, fairly and with evidence, that a trainee or employee is competent. Assessments test what people can do and explain, never only what they can memorise.

    Assessment principles

    • Evidence-based: judgement rests on reviewed work products, observed practice and oral explanation.
    • Second assessor: the assessor is not the trainee's buddy for the same piece of work.
    • No lowering of standards: pass marks are not reduced to meet schedules; coaching time is added instead.
    • Transparent: rubrics are shared before the assessment; feedback is written within three working days.
    • Re-assessment: one re-take after coaching; a second failure goes to the Test Manager for a development plan.

    Question banks with model answers

    The banks give core questions with model answers. Trainers extend them (with ISTQB-style sample questions and company scenarios) to at least 20 questions for the Level 1 quiz and 10 for every other gate, drawn randomly. Never reveal the model answers to trainees before assessment.

    Level 1 — Fundamentals

    #QuestionModel answer
    1What is the difference between quality assurance and quality control?QA is process-oriented and prevents defects (standards, reviews, training). QC is product-oriented and detects defects (testing, inspection).
    2Define error, defect and failure and give one example chain.A human error creates a defect in a work product; running it can cause a failure. Example: developer writes > instead of >= (error) → age check wrong (defect) → age 18 rejected (failure).
    3Verification versus validation?Verification: are we building the product right (against the specification)? Validation: are we building the right product (for user need)?
    4Why is exhaustive testing impossible, and what do we do instead?Input combinations, paths and environments are effectively unlimited. We use risk, priorities and techniques (EP, BVA) to choose the most valuable tests.
    5A headline on the home page has a spelling mistake two days before a major launch. Severity and priority?Low severity (cosmetic) but high priority (visible at launch; cheap to fix).
    6Who closes a defect, and when?The tester, only after verifying the fix on the named fixed build using the original steps, with evidence.
    7Name five of the seven testing principles.Testing shows presence of defects; exhaustive testing is impossible; early testing; defect clustering; pesticide paradox; context dependence; absence-of-defects fallacy (any five).
    8What makes an expected result good?Observable, specific, measurable and unambiguous (for example “message ‘Registration successful’ is displayed and the Login view opens”), not “works correctly”.

    Level 2 — Manual testing

    #QuestionModel answer
    1A field accepts ages 18 to 60 inclusive. Give the two-value boundary tests.17 (invalid), 18 (valid), 60 (valid), 61 (invalid). Three-value adds 19 and 59.
    2A password must be 8–20 characters. Which lengths do you test at the boundaries?7, 8, 20, 21 (plus 9 and 19 for three-value BVA), each combined with the other password rules.
    3Discount: below ₹1,000 none; ₹1,000–4,999 5 %; ₹5,000 or more 10 %. List partitions and boundary values.Partitions: <1,000; 1,000–4,999; ≥5,000. Boundaries: 999, 1,000, 4,999, 5,000 (plus a representative such as 500, 2,000, 7,000).
    4Explain smoke, sanity and regression testing.Smoke: broad, shallow check that the build is testable. Sanity: narrow check that a fix/change works. Regression: confirm existing behaviour still works after change.
    5What is a charter in exploratory testing?A short mission statement (what to explore, where, with what focus) for a time-boxed session (usually 60–90 minutes); results and notes are recorded.
    6When may a regression test be retired?When the feature is removed or the requirement changed, when it duplicates another test, or when it cannot be stabilised and its risk is covered otherwise — always with a recorded reason.
    7Give one entry and one exit criterion for test execution.Entry: build deployed, smoke test passed, test data loaded. Exit: all critical cases executed and no open Severity 1/2 defect without a written waiver.
    8Who decides whether UAT is accepted?The client's business owner. QA supports and reports; it does not decide business acceptance.

    Level 3 — Web and mobile

    #QuestionModel answer
    1Why are emulators not enough for mobile testing?They approximate hardware, performance, sensors, vendor OS modifications and real network behaviour; final verification needs real devices.
    2After logout you press the browser Back button. What must you verify?That no protected content is shown and the session is ended (redirect to login), including data in storage.
    3Which cookie attributes do you check on the session cookie?Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite, plus that the identifier changes at login and is cleared at logout.
    4What contrast ratio does WCAG AA require for normal-size text?At least 4.5 : 1 (3 : 1 for large text).
    5How do you choose the supported browser matrix?From the client's analytics, contract and risk — agreed in writing; not “all browsers”.
    6Name three keyboard-accessibility checks.Every function reachable and operable by keyboard; visible focus indicator; logical tab order; no keyboard trap; Esc closes dialogs.
    7A user double-clicks the Submit button. What do you verify?Only one request/record is created and the UI prevents duplicate submission (disabled button or idempotent handling).
    8What precaution do you take before sharing a HAR file?Remove tokens, cookies, personal data and other secrets, or share only a redacted copy through approved channels.

    Level 4 — API

    #QuestionModel answer
    1Which status for a request without a token, and which for a valid user lacking permission?401 Unauthorized for missing/invalid authentication; 403 Forbidden for authenticated but not permitted.
    2Which HTTP methods are idempotent?GET, PUT, DELETE (and HEAD, OPTIONS). POST is not; PATCH is not guaranteed.
    3You send DELETE twice for the same resource. What do you expect?First 204 (or 200); second 404 because the resource is already gone — unless the specification states otherwise.
    4Why add schema validation when you already check the status code?Schema checks catch missing fields, wrong types or extra fields (for example price returned as text) that a 200 status hides.
    5A malformed request causes a 500 response. What is your conclusion?A defect: client mistakes must produce a 4xx with a safe error body; 5xx indicates unhandled server behaviour and may leak internals.
    6Which header normally accompanies 201 Created?Location, giving the URL of the new resource.
    7How do you treat tokens in defect reports and repositories?Never include or commit them; redact in evidence; keep in environment variables or secret stores.
    8Explain safe versus idempotent.Safe: does not change server state (GET). Idempotent: repeating the request leaves the same state (PUT, DELETE). All safe methods are idempotent, not vice versa.

    Level 5 — Automation

    #QuestionModel answer
    1When is automating a manual test worth it?When (manual minutes per run × number of runs) exceeds (build time + maintenance), the test is stable, repeatable and has a precise expected result.
    2Why must you avoid fixed sleeps?They make tests slow and flaky; use auto-waiting actions and web-first assertions or explicit waits on conditions.
    3In the Page Object Model, where do assertions go?In the tests. Page objects hold locators and actions only.
    4What is the purpose of xfail(strict=True) with a defect ID?Records a known defect as an expected failure; when fixed, the test passes and strict mode fails the run so the marker is removed and the defect closed.
    5Where do credentials for CI tests live?In the CI secret store / environment variables — never in code, YAML or the repository.
    6What does test independence mean?Each test creates its own data and can run alone, in any order and in parallel.
    7Which locators do you prefer?Role, label, text or dedicated test ids; avoid positional XPath and long CSS chains.
    8How do you detect a flaky test?Rerun it many times (e.g. 10) on the same commit, run in random/parallel order, inspect traces; any inconsistent result marks it flaky.

    Level 6 — Advanced QA

    #QuestionModel answer
    1Why report percentiles rather than the average response time?Averages hide the slow tail; p95/p99 show what the worst-affected users experience.
    2Using N = X × R, how many concurrent sessions arise from 2 new sessions per second lasting 90 s?N = 2 × 90 = 180 concurrent sessions.
    3Differentiate load, stress, spike and soak tests.Load: expected peak. Stress: beyond peak to the breaking point. Spike: sudden surge. Soak: long duration to find leaks/degradation.
    4Where may you run a performance test?Only in an environment authorised in writing, under controlled conditions with monitoring and a stop contact — not production or third-party systems without explicit approval.
    5What is QA's role in security testing?Run agreed safe checks, escalate observations privately to the named security coordinator, retest fixes and report risk; never exploit or probe beyond the authorised scope.
    6Write the idea of a SQL check for orphan records.LEFT JOIN child to parent and select child rows where the parent key IS NULL; expected result: zero rows.
    7Does 100 % code coverage prove quality?No. It shows lines executed, not that behaviour is asserted correctly or that requirements are covered.
    8State the flaky-test policy.Detect by rerun; log in the register; quarantine ≤ 10 working days; fix or delete; report the flaky rate; retries must be counted and reported.

    Metrics, costing and conduct

    #QuestionModel answer
    1450 cases planned; 360 passed, 40 failed, 20 blocked, 30 not run. Calculate execution % and pass rate.Executed = 400 → execution % = 400 ÷ 450 = 88.9 %. Pass rate = 360 ÷ 400 = 90.0 %.
    245 defects found in QA and 5 after release. Calculate defect leakage.5 ÷ (45 + 5) = 10 %.
    3Delivery cost is ₹3,00,000 and the target gross margin is 40 %. What price do you quote?Price = 3,00,000 ÷ (1 − 0.40) = ₹5,00,000 (before taxes).
    4The client asks you to mark blocked tests as “passed” to hit a target. What do you do?Refuse, explain the metric formula, report blocked tests honestly, and escalate to the QA Lead/Test Manager if pressure continues.
    5You discover a client's password in a screenshot you committed. What do you do?Tell the QA Lead immediately, have the secret revoked/rotated, remove it per the approved procedure, record an incident note.

    Final practical assessment (60 marks)

    TaskMarksStandard
    Design and execute 10 test cases on an unseen build with seeded defects15At least 60 % of seeded defects found; reports reproducible
    Automate 3 UI and 3 API checks from a written specification15Clean code; independent tests; green run
    Prepare a release QA summary from supplied raw data15Metrics recomputed correctly; honest risk statement
    Oral examination (15 minutes)15Explains choices; handles ethics scenarios (metric pressure, secrets, authorisation)
    Ethics scenarios are mandatory in the oral exam

    At least two scenarios from: pressure to change a severity, request to test an unauthorised system, discovery of production data in a test environment, a metric that can be improved by a shortcut, a committed secret. A trainee who would compromise integrity does not pass, whatever their technical score.

    20. Templates and QA Sign-off Checklist

    Controlled templates for every document in the lifecycle. Copy the Markdown or CSV version from qa-project-template/ into the project repository; the forms below show the required fields. Grey hint text describes what to enter — delete it when filling in.

    How to use a template
    • Copy it, fill every field or write “N/A — reason”; never leave a field silently blank.
    • Keep the header block (ID, version, status, author, reviewer, date) and update it on every change.
    • Store the file in the path shown; commit with a message such as docs(test-plan): v0.2 add risks.
    • Evidence and attachments are referenced by file name or link, with secrets removed.

    10. LimitationsWhat these results do not prove.

    QA sign-off checklist

    Complete before every release recommendation (Stage 14). Every box ticked needs a reference to evidence; the second reviewer re-checks a sample.

    Scope and plan

    • Approved test strategy and plan are in the repository, versioned.
    • Scope changes since approval are recorded and approved.
    • Entry criteria were met before execution began (Gate G6).

    Execution

    • All planned critical cases executed; counts reconcile (passed + failed + blocked + not run = planned).
    • Every result has evidence; evidence contains no secrets or personal data.
    • Regression exit criteria met (Gate G12).

    Defects

    • All Severity 1 and 2 defects are fixed and verified, or waived in writing by the product owner.
    • Every deferred defect is in the risk summary with an owner.
    • No defect was closed without a verified retest.

    Coverage and automation

    • Requirement coverage computed and uncovered requirements listed.
    • Automation results attached; flaky tests reported separately.
    • Known defects marked as expected failures reference defect IDs.

    Non-functional

    • Performance report approved, with limitations stated (or explicitly out of scope).
    • Accessibility findings listed against WCAG criteria (or out of scope).
    • Security observations handed to the named coordinator.

    UAT and release

    • UAT acceptance signed (or not required by contract).
    • Production smoke list, accounts, window and rollback decision-maker agreed.
    • Second reviewer checked numbers against raw data.

    Records

    • Metrics have formulas, dates, builds and sources.
    • Recommendation is Go / Conditional Go / No-Go and follows from the evidence.
    • Evidence is archived per the retention rule; no real customer data exists in the repository.

    C. Daily tester checklist

    • Read yesterday's journal entry and today's plan; confirm the build number.
    • Smoke test passed before deeper execution.
    • Every executed case has a result and evidence.
    • Every failure reproduced twice and logged before end of day.
    • No secrets or personal data in evidence or messages.
    • Blockers raised in stand-up, not at the end of the week.
    • Journal entry written and committed.

    D. Pre-submission checklist for any deliverable

    • Header block complete: ID, version, status, author, reviewer, date.
    • All numbers re-computed from raw data by me and by a reviewer.
    • Every claim has evidence or is marked as an assumption.
    • Gaps and untested areas stated plainly.
    • Spelling and terminology consistent with the glossary.
    • Saved at the correct repository path and committed with a clear message.

    E. Glossary

    TermMeaning
    Acceptance criteriaConditions a feature must satisfy to be accepted by the client.
    Boundary-value analysis (BVA)Technique testing values at and next to the edges of valid ranges.
    BuildA specific compiled/packaged version of the software under test.
    CI/CDContinuous integration / delivery: automated build, test and deployment on every change.
    Defect (bug)A flaw in a work product that can cause a failure.
    Defect leakageShare of defects that escape QA and are found after release.
    Entry / exit criteriaConditions to start / finish a test activity.
    Equivalence partitioning (EP)Technique that groups inputs treated the same and tests one value per group.
    Exploratory testingSimultaneous learning, test design and execution guided by a charter.
    FailureObservable deviation of actual from expected behaviour.
    FixtureReusable setup/teardown code supplied to tests.
    Flaky testA test that passes and fails on the same code without changes.
    IdempotentRepeating the operation leaves the system in the same state.
    JSON SchemaA standard vocabulary for describing and validating JSON structure.
    Page Object ModelDesign pattern that wraps page locators and actions in classes.
    Percentile (p95)Value below which the stated percentage of measurements fall.
    Regression testingRe-testing to ensure changes did not break existing functionality.
    Requirements Traceability MatrixTable mapping requirements to tests, results and defects.
    Risk-based testingChoosing and prioritising tests by the likelihood and impact of failure.
    Sanity testingNarrow check that a specific change or fix works.
    Severity / priorityTechnical impact of a defect / business urgency to fix it.
    Smoke testingBroad, shallow check that a build is stable enough to test.
    SLAService-level agreement: measurable service commitments.
    Test case / scenario / suiteA precise verification / a high-level condition / a collection of cases.
    Test environmentHardware, software, data and configuration in which tests run.
    ThroughputRequests or transactions processed per unit time.
    UATUser acceptance testing by the client's business users.
    Virtual user (VU)A simulated user in a load test.
    WCAGWeb Content Accessibility Guidelines published by the W3C.
    xfailpytest marker for a test expected to fail because of a known defect.
